In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Consortium Project Manager Colombia Bogota
body:
All NRC employees are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s core values: dedication, innovation, inclusivity, and accountability. These attitudes and beliefs shall guide our actions and relationships.

## What we are looking for

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a **highly qualified,** **resilient, and dynamic professional** to take up the role of **Consortium Manager – Emergency Response** for Colombia. The purpose of the position is to **ensure MIRE+ emergency and early recovery responses are implemented with quality, in a coordinated and timely manner, in compliance with donors and partners’ strategies and policies and in accordance to target populations’ needs in a rapidly evolving context. The Consortium Manager should strive to maintain MIRE+ positive reputation as Colombia’s largest rapid response mechanism, always seeking to improve technical and operational processes to achieve optimal efficiency and quality in the response. He/She should show leadership and adaptability as well as strong problem-solving skills and positive, assertive communication capacities.**

## What you will do

1. Provide overall direction and leadership of the Consortium to ensure seamless operations, leveraging complementarity among multi-disciplinary partners.
2. Ensure day-to-day strategic and operational coordination with NRC management leadership as leader of the consortium.
3. Oversee day-to-day management of the project, including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and budget spending, ensuring the project is always on scope and schedule.
4. Represent the Consortium towards relevant stakeholders, including national authorities, donors, humanitarian country team and counterparts, promoting the best interests of the Consortium.
5. Line manager and supervise the work of the Consortium Management Unit; carry out any needed recruitment, including consultants.
6. Lead the consultations, design and preparation of the next strategic cycle of the Consortium based on evidenced needs, donor expectations and drawing from partners’ diverse expertise.
7. Contribute to fundraising initiatives to diversify the Consortium’s portfolio, actively seeking new relationships with donors and developing funding proposals.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCGbGBJjy3XS5T_HgandSoAAewHPGz5AdIi2R2sH6YMgYs?e=rWpSar)to learn more about the position.

What you will bring

- Minimum 5-7 years of experience in the sector, with progressively increasing responsibilities in humanitarian crises’ contexts.
- At least three of those years in a leadership position involving the management and coordination of similarly sized, international donor supported programmes.
- Proven ability to communicate a common vision among diverse partners and the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams.
- Experience in complex and volatile settings.
- Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish.
- Knowledge and experience of working in Latin America is strongly preferred. Specific knowledge and experience of the context in Colombia is desirable.
- Demonstrated experience in emergency response management and international best practice.
- Well-versed in humanitarian architecture in the region.
- Knowledge of the particular dynamics of ethnic communities and regulatory frameworks.
- University Degree in International Development, Social or Human Sciences, Project Management, Emergency Response or related field.

## What we offer

- **Duty station: Bogotá, Colombia** (with extensive travel within the country)
- **Contract: national or international contract**
- Travel: up to 30%
- Salary/benefits**: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale**, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

## Important information about the application process

- *Internal candidates only: please click on the suitcase icon labelled “I am an employee” to be redirected to NRC’s internal careers site.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email aela.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line.

## Why NRC?

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We contribute to the development of policy aiming to protect the rights of the displaced and we call for increased humanitarian funding and engagement on processes that will generate structural changes in protection and assistance in the region.

NRC implements a multi-country Colombia-Panama-Ecuador strategy to respond to the complex crises and emergencies across the sub-continent. In Colombia, we provide assistance to IDPs and victims of the armed conflict in hard-to-reach areas where authorities struggle to protect civilians and provide help. We also help Colombians in need of international protection in Ecuador and Panama, as well as Venezuelans who were triggered to flee their country as a result of the growing political instability and humanitarian crisis. We provide protection, legal assistance, education, livelihoods and food security, WASH and shelter services to affected populations.

Within this context, NRC leads an intersectoral Rapid Response Mechanism (MIRE+ consortium) together with Action Against Hunger (ACF), Médecins du Monde (MdM) and Pastoral Social - Cáritas Colombia funded by EU Humanitarian Aid (ECHO), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the Spanish Agency for International Development (AECID) and Swiss Development Cooperation (COSUDE/SDC). Under a triple nexus framework, the consortium delivers multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance responding rapidly to emergencies resulting from the armed conflict in Colombia, natural hazards and early recovery activities. MIRE+ operates across all the country, prioritizing response in hard-to-reach areas and bringing support to people that have been affected by multiple compounding crises. The consortium has just entered a new two-year strategic cycle. We are therefore searching for an experienced and dynamic Chief of Party to lead the multi-donor emergency and early recovery Consortium. Whilst this position is hosted by NRC, the Consortium Manager will represent the MIRE+.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

### About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: External Auditor for JRS Project
Director of Advocacy
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview:**   
As the Director of Advocacy, you will lead development of the IRC’s advocacy efforts to support key priorities across crisis and solutions-driven global influence priorities for the International Rescue Committee. You are responsible for crafting our influence strategies using IRC’s programmatic and research evidence, surgical policy and practice solutions, and trusted brand to inspire collective action. You are the expert for understanding current federal legislative and policy trends in the US and how our policies cut across political agendas. You will engage key stakeholders across government and civil society. You will work across the IRC to develop advocacy campaigns and build relationships including with Congressional representatives, U.S. and other government officials in D.C. as well as foundations, think tanks, multilateral organizations, and other humanitarian organizations. You will also look across IRC’s global priorities, engaging relevant embassies and crafting specific advocacy messages for donor governments.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Advocacy Strategy:** Lead advocacy strategies for specific policy goals, including thought leadership objectives relevant to the U.S. market, collaborating with policy leads to advance IRCs key influence priorities and maximize the opportunity for IRC to advance our influence objectives. Engage across the IRC with all relevant stakeholders. Craft advocacy strategies, drawing on IRC’s policy expertise, that are suited to global donor government priorities.
- **Influence Analysis:** Develop U.S. power maps for key policy issues to identify influence priorities. Cultivate relationships across the U.S. Government and lead Congressional engagement. Work with team to support development and execution of creative influence strategies, including with nontraditional partners. Look across IRC’s global priorities and ensure they are integrated into advocacy and influence strategies.
- **Advocacy:** Support efforts to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships by engaging with key policy stakeholders and supporting opportunities to raise IRC’s profile at key meetings and fora. Collaborate closely with other U.S. market staff and global policy and advocacy staff, contributing to efforts designed to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships in Washington.
- Legislative and Policy Tracking. Expand IRC’s legislative reach by tracking and analyzing shifting Congressional and Executive branch positions, individuals engaging on our issues, and the politics around our issues. Translate policy asks into legislative asks. Engage U.S. Government stakeholders relevant to the IRC’s work in the U.S. Track U.S. legislative and executive processes.
- **Policy Engagement:** Contribute to policy generation by providing U.S.-specific analysis that increases the credibility and efficacy of our solutions through constant collaboration. Support IRC’s policy team in identifying and developing policy priorities that are impactful and achievable in the U.S. as well as in global markets.
- **Communications:** Provide market and audience expertise to communications team to shape policy communications specific to the U.S.Support the team in developing communications strategy and develop materials for advocacy targets. Support planning and implementation of strategic activities including events. Facilitate development and editing of internal and external advocacy products to ensure resonance in U.S. market and adherence to high standards of quality.
- **Steward Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** both in the culture of IRC, as well as in the policy solutions we develop and the ways we wield influence.
- **Spokesperson:** Act as an IRC influence spokespersonon focused advocacy areas. Act as key interlocutor with legislative and governmental staffers**.**
- **Board and Advisors:** Support relationships with IRC's Board and Advisors by identifying points of mutual interest and opportunities around our priority issues.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Potential supervision of Senior Advisor or other staff.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Senior Director, Advocacy & Influence and Vice President of Policy and Advocacy
- **Internal contacts:** Policy and Advocacy colleagues across the globe; Technical Excellence leads; International Programs leads; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Communications; Awards Management; President’s Office, External Relations Department
- **External contacts:** Key Opinion Formers and policy makers in the U.S. Government and U.S. Congress, other humanitarian leaders and thinktanks, relevant embassies, multilateral institutions

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Degree in relevant field such as Public Policy, Law or International Relations

***Work experience:***

- Demonstrated experience in advocacy and advocacy strategy development with a focus on creativity and strategic thinking
- 10-12 years of experience working on complex humanitarian and/or development issues
- Knowledge of U.S. Government functioning and prior work the U.S. Government or Congress are a plus.
- Understanding of global issues, multilateral engagement experience.

***Demonstrated skills and competencies:***

- Examples of influence/impact on legislative and executive policy. Strong network of influencers and policy makers
- Deep understanding of global issues related to the humanitarian field.
- Ability to think strategically and creatively, being solutions-oriented
- Extensive knowledge of humanitarian aid and refugee issues, particularly around the complex drivers of humanitarian need
- Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate successfully with experts, high level decision and policy makers, and colleagues in the humanitarian and development fields. Good public speaking skills.
- Excellent writing skills and the ability to translate complex material and data into coherent narratives that resonate with policymakers
- Fluency with key parts of the IRC’s strategy and existing policy strategy
- Ability to work on tight deadlines and juggle competing demands
- Self-motivated

**Working Environment:** Remote

**Compensation:** ***($130,000 - $156,000 - annually).*** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Head of Programmes CARE Ukraine
body:
## **Is this you?**

**Contract Start Date**: early 2027, no later than 1 March, 2027  
**Contract Duration:** 1 year  
**Duty Station:** Kyiv (Ukraine)

As a member of the Senior Management Team, reporting directly to the Country Director, the Head of Programmes leads the development and implementation of high-quality programmes in Ukraine, ensuring delivery against scope, time and budget, and overseeing quality management and impact across the portfolio. The role line-manages the Programme Implementation Lead, Technical Advisors and Coordinators, and MEAL Coordinator, while ensuring close cross-departmental coordination. It places particular emphasis on programme quality and strengthening partners’ technical capacities in relevant sectors. Working closely with the Country Director, Programme Development Lead, Partnership Coordinator, Advocacy Advisor and department heads, the Head of Programmes contributes to strategic direction, programme implementation and partnership development.

## **Your mission**

## Overall Programme Implementation and Quality

- Provide inclusive and cohesive leadership to CARE Ukraine’s programme teams, ensuring coordinated, high-quality implementation in line with the Country Strategy.
- Maintain a strong understanding of Ukraine’s social, political and economic context, initiating assessments to identify emerging needs and opportunities for programme expansion.
- Ensure projects are delivered on scope, time and budget, with day-to-day oversight delegated to the Program Implementation Lead and technical guidance provided by relevant teams.
- Regularly review programme priorities against the Country Strategy, adapting them based on contextual changes, evidence, learning and priorities identified with partners.
- Ensure effective coordination between programme implementation, technical teams, MEAL and Program Development to address challenges, strengthen cross-sector integration and inform new initiatives.
- Oversee strategic programmes and initiatives, ensuring their contribution to CARE Ukraine’s long-term objectives.
- Mainstream gender equality, protection and inclusion across all programmes, ensuring consistent application of CARE’s programme quality standards.
- Lead regular programme review meetings covering progress, quality, risks and monitoring findings, ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
- Resolve operational bottlenecks between the Programme Department and other Country and Area Office departments.

## Oversight and Management of Programme Implementation and Budget

- In collaboration with the SMT, define and oversee an effective, efficient and sustainable programme implementation model, clarifying the roles of CARE and its partners and ensuring appropriate SOPs and systems are in place.
- Support the Partnership Coordinator in overseeing partner due diligence, capacity development plans and partnership agreements, ensuring compliance with CARE requirements, including PSEA.
- Ensure effective use and follow-up of project management tools, including Detailed Implementation Plans, MEAL Plans and monitoring reports, through the Program Implementation Lead and MEAL Coordinator.
- Ensure programmes are responsive to communities, particularly women and girls, and comply with CARE’s principles, values, strategic plans and CI procedures.
- Act as overall budget holder for all programmes, delegating day-to-day budget management to the Program Implementation Lead while retaining accountability for expenditure and donor compliance.
- Oversee financial forecasting, expenditure monitoring and corrective actions, ensuring budget risks and variances are addressed and resources are aligned with programme priorities, in coordination with Finance and Operations.
- Provide direction on significant budget adjustments and resource allocation, and directly oversee specific grants where required.

## Programme Quality, Technical Support and Learning

- Maintain and adapt CARE Ukraine’s programme quality framework in line with CARE International and humanitarian standards, including the Core Humanitarian Standard.
- Guide technical leads in ensuring compliance with minimum technical standards and consistent application of appropriate tools, guidelines and SOPs, providing the necessary support to Programme Managers and partners.
- Promote coherent and integrated technical approaches across sectors, particularly regarding gender equality, protection and inclusion.
- Lead regular programme quality reviews with technical teams, MEAL and the Program Implementation Lead, ensuring gaps, risks and improvement actions are identified and addressed.
- Oversee MEAL and information management systems through the MEAL Coordinator, ensuring reliable and timely evidence on programme quality and outcomes and addressing significant system and capacity gaps.
- Set priorities for needs assessments, evaluations, external monitoring and research, ensuring their quality and relevance to programme effectiveness and changing needs.
- Lead the development of a research and learning agenda with MEAL and technical teams, ensuring evidence, implementation experience and good practices inform technical approaches and programme adaptation.
- Ensure learning and recommendations are shared with CARE teams and partners, translated into improvements and reflected in programme strategy.
- Oversee CARE Ukraine’s accountability mechanism, ensuring community feedback informs programme reviews and adaptations in line with CARE standards.
- Ensure partner capacity strengthening addresses identified quality gaps and its effectiveness is regularly reviewed with technical leads and the Partnership Unit.

## Business Development

- Support the Country Director in developing and adapting the funding strategy, diversifying donor engagement in line with CARE Ukraine’s Country Strategy.
- Coordinate technical inputs to new programmes, proposals and reports with the Program Development Lead, Program Implementation Lead, technical teams and MEAL Coordinator, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and quality standards.
- Ensure programme design builds on contextual analysis, monitoring findings, lessons learned and priorities identified with communities and partners.
- Promote the meaningful participation of partners and communities in programme design, including the development of logical frameworks, activities and budgets, ensuring proposals address identified needs and include appropriate MEAL components and resources.

## Representation and Networking

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with strategic and implementing partners and peer organisations.
- Maintain strong links across CARE International and its membership to mobilise technical expertise and resources in support of the Country Strategy.
- Engage with UN agencies, humanitarian clusters and sector working groups to inform strategic priorities and operational planning, share programme evidence and learning, and fulfil CARE’s coordination commitments, including co-leadership responsibilities.
- Provide programme evidence and technical input to advocacy and communications strategies, working closely with the Advocacy Advisor and Communications Coordinator to promote the visibility and uptake of programme learning.

## Team Management and Coordination

- Manage the performance and development of direct reports in line with CARE policies, providing coaching, mentoring and training to strengthen leadership and team effectiveness.
- Oversee recruitment, training and promotion of programme staff, ensuring that key functions are adequately staffed.
- Foster a collaborative and respectful team environment, promoting staff resilience and well-being in challenging contexts.
- Identify staff capacity development needs in collaboration with Human Resources.
- Supervise managers and technical leads, ensuring coordinated implementation of workplans and budgets.
- Lead safeguarding prevention and response across CARE Ukraine’s workplaces, programmes and communities, ensuring compliance with CARE standards and policies on PSEA-CP, Gender Equality and CARE Performance Standards, in coordination with the CARE DE Safeguarding Focal Point and CARE Ukraine HR Manager.

## **Your profile**

**Essential**  
**Experience and Technical Expertise**

- At least 7 years’ experience in humanitarian and/or development work with national or international NGOs, including 5 years in senior management roles and significant field operations experience.
- At least 2 years’ experience living and working in an emergency or conflict setting.
- Master’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences or a relevant discipline.
- Good understanding of at least one of CARE’s key programme sectors (Protection, WASH/Shelter, SRH or Livelihoods).
- Strong knowledge of international humanitarian and development systems, institutions and donors.
- Proven project management skills, including knowledge of accountability frameworks and substantial experience in financial and budgetary management.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender equality and gender-transformative programming.
- Sound understanding of MEAL systems and experience using data, evidence and learning to assess programme quality, adapt implementation and inform programme design.
- Experience in partnership-based approaches, civil society development and strengthening the capacity of local partner organisations.

**Leadership and Management Skills**

- Proven ability to lead, motivate and develop teams through coaching, mentoring and capacity building, including cross-functional teams.
- Strong results orientation, with the ability to challenge existing approaches and drive improvements.
- Excellent analytical and strategic thinking skills, including the ability to assess information, evaluate options and plan effectively.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, negotiation and influencing skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Ability and willingness to work flexible hours and operate in environments with security restrictions.
- Strong commitment to CARE’s mission, values and principles.
- High levels of political and cultural sensitivity, patience, tact and diplomacy.
- Strong sense of responsibility, integrity and trustworthiness.

**Desirable**

- Significant experience designing and supporting partner-led programmes.
- Strong and up-to-date knowledge of the humanitarian context in Ukraine.
- Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or other relevant regional languages.
- Experience in training and capacity development.
- Proven representation and networking skills, including the ability to represent CARE effectively in external forums.

## **Why us?**

CARE Ukraine is a country office which comes under the management of CARE Germany. It has been operating in Ukraine since March 2022.

CARE prioritizes a locally led response and is partnering primarily with Civil-Society Organizations (CSOs), National NGOs, local authorities, and when needed, INGOs with a longstanding presence in the country and access to hard-to-reach areas. CARE Ukraine deliberately and strategically prioritizes partnerships with local and national Women Led and Women Rights organizations (WLO’s/ WRO’s), in accordance with Gender in Emergencies (GiE) principles.

CARE Ukraine’s FY25 portfolio was approx. EUR 13 million, funded by GFFO/ BMZ, ECHO, DANIDA, Czech MOFA, ADA (Austrian Development Agency), AFD (Agence Francaise de Developpement), LDS (Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints) and others. We implement primarily humanitarian programs, in the protection/ GBV, SRH, integrated humanitarian response and WASH/ shelter sectors. Some 10-15% of our programs are recovery/ response, primarily in livelihoods, WASH and womens empowerment sectors. The focus of most programming is the frontline oblasts of Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, and Dnipropetrovsk oblast. We also have some programming in Odesa. The country office is in Kyiv, with a support office in Lviv and field offices in Dnipro and Kharkiv. We plan to phase out the Lviv support office in the second half of 2026.

CARE Ukraine currently partners with 12 local/national organizations, almost all of which are WLO’s/WRO’s. We channel some 80% of our funding through local/national partners. Through the activities that have been implemented so far, CARE Ukraine has been able to reach over 750,000 people, including IDPs and affected populations in hard-to-reach areas.

## **General information**

CARE values equal opportunities and diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.

**Accountability within CARE**  
A commitment to CARE values and CARE’s integrity framework is critical to working with CARE. Any candidate offered a job with CARE will be expected to adhere to the following key areas of accountability:  
\- Comply with CARE’s policies and procedures with respect to safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, confidentiality, do no harm principles and unacceptable behavior protocols.  
\- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.  
\- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior of a CARE staff or partner.

**Safeguarding**  
Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with CARE as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that CARE shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Gender equality**  
CARE is committed to meeting the standards of the CARE International Gender Policy (2019). Through this policy, CARE seeks to promote the equal realization of dignity and human rights for girls, women, boys and men in all diversities, and the elimination of poverty and injustice. Specifically, this policy seeks to improve the explicit incorporation of gender in programmatic and organizational practices.

## **Our offer**

- Competitive salary
- Housing allowance
- Risk allowance
- Relocation package
- Vacation according to the country office policies, plus additional days off on public holidays
- Generous R&R policy
- 24/7 group accident insurance
- Health insurance
- Coverage of relevant training and development opportunities

We are looking for highly motivated team members who identify with CARE’s goals and values. We offer a varied role with numerous employee benefits within a supportive, international team.

## **About us**

**About CARE Germany**  
Founded in 1980 and based in Bonn, CARE Germany is a member of the CARE International confederation—a global humanitarian network dedicated to fighting poverty and delivering life-saving aid in times of crisis. We work with communities to promote sustainable development, gender equality, and resilience, addressing the world’s most pressing challenges from climate change to conflict-driven displacement.  
At CARE Germany, our staff are the cornerstone of our humanitarian efforts. Committed to the principles of CARE International and working tirelessly to uplift disadvantaged communities worldwide. Whether based in our headquarters or in our Country Offices in the Balkans, Ukraine, Iraq, or Libya, each team member plays a vital role in delivering aid, supporting long-term recovery, and advocating for those most in need. Regardless of their role, all staff contribute to a collective mission—one rooted in solidarity, compassion, and impactful action.

title: Endline Evaluation-ReDSS Kenya Evidence Platform- Consultancy
body:
ReDSS is a secretariat working on behalf of 14 international and national NGOs responding to forced displacement in East Africa, the Horn of Africa and the Great Lakes region. ReDSS was established in 2015 in response to a desire by the NGO community to be more proactive in shaping durable solutions policy and programming in the region. Our team works both at regional and country level and focusses on the translation of evidence and research into policies and programmes that can better deliver for displacement-affected communities. This is achieved through a range of activities, including convening key stakeholders at multiple levels to build consensus around collective actions; supporting new evidence generation through commissioning and undertaking research and analysis; and building the capacity of key actors through delivering training and developing tools and guidance among others.

## Project Background

The Kenya Evidence Platform (KEP) was established in response to a persistent gap within the displacement sector: the limited visibility and uptake of refugee-led and locally grounded research within refugee policy and programming processes in Kenya. Funded by the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the three-year initiative (2023–2026) operates at the intersection of research, policy, and practice, with a focus on strengthening locally driven evidence generation and use.

Implemented by a consortium comprising the Regional Durable Solutions Secretariat (ReDSS), the Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH), and Maseno University, KEP was launched during a significant period of policy transition in Kenya, including the implementation of the Refugees Act (2021) and the development and launch of the Shirika Plan. Within this context, the platform seeks to strengthen the role of refugee and Kenyan researchers in shaping evidence-informed approaches to refugee management and durable solutions.

KEP has supported a range of initiatives aimed at strengthening the refugee research ecosystem in Kenya. These include:

- Supporting refugee and Kenyan scholars to produce independent research papers and evidence products;
- Establishing and supporting the Forced Migration Research Network in Kenya (FOMREK) to strengthen coordination, mentorship, and collaboration among researchers;
- Conducting research trainings, coaching, and mentorship for emerging refugee and local researchers;
- Convening policy dialogues and engagement forums involving government, academia, humanitarian and development actors; and
- Producing and disseminating evidence products intended to inform refugee policy and programming in Kenya.

The platform primarily targets researchers with lived experience of displacement, Kenyan scholars, academia, policymakers, and actors involved in refugee policy and programming, particularly in Nairobi, Kakuma, and Dadaab.

Through these interventions, KEP aims to contribute to improved coordination around refugee research, increased availability and visibility of refugee-led evidence, stronger research capacity among emerging scholars, and more direct engagement between evidence producers and decisionmakers within Kenya’s refugee management ecosystem.

## Purpose of the consultancy

The primary purpose of this consultancy is to conduct a rigorous, utilization-focused endline evaluation. Given the absence of a formal baseline at project inception and the operational unfeasibility of non-treatment comparison groups, the evaluation utilizes a Theory-Based framework that fulfills three distinct evaluative functions:

- **Strategic Accountability:** Verifying performance beyond output counts by evaluating the technical quality and policy relevance of research products (via standardized qualitative rubrics), tracing the depth of institutional evidence uptake in key policy frameworks (example: Shirika Plan, Differentiated Assistance Framework, County Integrated Development Plans, etc.), and independently substantiating behavioural outcomes among target decision-makers.
- **Baseline Reconstruction & Capacity Trajectory Mapping:** Reconstructing historical capacity starting points, specifically for supported researchers using single-sitting Retrospective Pre-Test (RPT) self-assessments, anchored and validated through objective rubric-based scoring of pre- vs. post-project research artifacts (e.g., initial concept notes vs. Published working papers/briefs) across distinct exposure tiers.
- **Learning & Systems Tracing:** Identifying the qualitative mechanisms, institutional pathways, and contextual drivers (e.g., political incentives, funding shifts, regional coordination structures) that facilitated or hindered the uptake of refugee-led and locally grounded research within Kenya's forced displacement architecture.

## Objective of the consultancy

The specific objectives of the endline evaluation are:

1. **Assess Research Quality & Production (Outcome 1):** Determine the extent to which the platform increased the production of high-quality, locally authored research products, evaluating their academic and technical rigor using standardized qualitative rubrics.
2. **Evaluate Policy and Programmatic Influence (Outcome 3):** Trace the utilization of KEP evidence products (policy briefs, research papers, Evidence Mapping Reports) within government bodies, humanitarian agencies, and NGO coordination mechanisms, assessing their specific influence on policy, practice outcomes and programme design.
3. **Reconstruct Tiered Capacity Trajectories (Outcome 2):** Measure changes in technical research skills, policy engagement capacity, and professional networking among supported researchers, disaggregated by category/tier of support (e.g., Independent Research Projects vs. Writing Workshops vs. Training Cohorts), using retrospective self-assessments triangulated against objective artifact quality scores.
4. **Analyze Systemic Localization (Cross-cutting):** Evaluate the project's contribution to increased visibility, credibility, institutional leadership (e.g., FOMREK), and structural inclusion of refugee-led and locally grounded researchers within Kenya's displacement architecture.
5. **Provide Strategic Recommendations (Learning):** Offer actionable, user-specific insights for the Kingdom of the Netherlands (DGIS), ReDSS, consortium partners, and local government actors on sustaining platform gains beyond the current funding cycle.

## Methodology & Scope of Work

**NOTE: The Methodology shared here is not prescriptive, the applicants are encouraged to propose a different approach, integrate with other approaches that deliver the results the consultancy is looking for or adapt it altogether. If adapted, the consultants will be at liberty to refine it during the inception phase.**

**Additional Note: The Project's Theory of Change already exists with highlighted Assumptions. The Total Project Participants after removal of duplicities are 789 (Nairobi, Kakuma, Dadaab (20%)). Total Project Evidence Products: 12**

This evaluation will utilize an **Integrated Theory-Based Evaluation (TBE) Framework**. Bidders are explicitly instructed **not** to propose quasi-experimental designs or non-treatment comparison groups, as these are unviable given the population parameters. Bidders must demonstrate methodological mastery in the following four core pillars:

**Core Methodological Pillars**

1. **Contribution Analysis (CA) with Process Tracing:**
    - The evaluation will use Mayne’s Contribution Analysis to test the project's vertical Theory of Change (ToC) logic and claims
    - During the Inception Phase, the consultant will explicitly reconstruct and disaggregate implicit ToC assumptions (these are generated from an already existing ToC) into testable capacity, behavioural, and contextual hypotheses.
    - For major policy and practice outcome claims, the consultant will apply qualitative Process Tracing tests to evaluate KEP’s contribution against rival hypotheses (e.g., independent Shirika Plan political momentum, World Bank/UNHCR funding shifts, or broader economic trends).
2. **Inductive Outcome Harvesting (OH) with Independent Substantiation:**
    - OH, will identify intended and unintended changes in the behaviour, relationships, policies, or practices of external social actors (government officials, UN agencies, RLOs, INGOs).
    - **Strict Methodological & Safeguarding Requirement:** Site-based Outcome Harvesting workshops in Nairobi, Kakuma, and Dadaab are strictly for *outcome formulation and discovery*. All outcome substantiation must be conducted independently via 1-on-1 external Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) or documentary verification.
3. **Tiered Within-Subject Capacity Mapping & Rubric Artifact Scoring:** To account for varying intervention intensity, the consultant must partition the beneficiary population into explicit **Exposure Tiers** rather than aggregating them into a single average:
    - *Tier 1 (High Intensity - IRP Grantees & Mentees):* Evaluated via qualitative 1-on-1 narrative KIIs, retrospective skill recall grids, and **objective rubric-based scoring of baseline vs. endline research artifacts** (comparing early proposals against final published papers/briefs using a 4-point qualitative quality rubric).
    - *Tier 2 (Medium Intensity - Writing Workshop Alumni):* Evaluated via retrospective self-assessment grids cross-checked against independent publication/submission verification.
    - *Tier 3 (Low Intensity - Training Cohort Alumni & Event Attendees):* Evaluated via lightweight tracer surveys focusing strictly on skill application, evidence reach, and immediate utility.

**Phased Scope of Work**

**The Note on the Methodology applies here as well.**

**Phase 1: Inception Phase (Days 1–10):** Inception Report, Reconstructing Theory of Change assumptions for CA; drafting quality rubrics for artifact scoring; designing modular, stakeholder-specific KII guides; and the Outcome Register template.

**Phase 2: Fieldwork & Independent Substantiation (Days 11–40):** Administering tiered quantitative/qualitative surveys to treated participants; conducting site-based OH workshops; conducting independent 1-on-1 substantiation KIIs with stakeholders

**Phase 3: Synthesis, Validation & Reporting (Days 40-60):** Triangulating qualitative narratives, rubric scores, and citation depth metrics; conducting participatory member-checking validation sessions with refugee researchers; drafting the final report; and producing the Policy & Programme Influence Map.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will be requested to submit the following deliverables:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Inception**

**Inception Report & Tools**

Detailed Workplan ; Reconstructed Theory of Change Assumptions/Hypotheses for CA ; Tiered Survey & Modular KII Guides ; Rubric-Based Artifact Scoring Template ; Manual Document Audit Protocol ; and Preliminary Outcome Register

10 days

**Data Collection/Fieldwork**

**Raw Data & Interim Update**

Completion of modular KIIs, site-based OH formulation workshops, independent 1-on-1 substantiation KIIs, treated-population survey; raw anonymized datasets, transcripts, and updated Outcome Register.

15 days

**Analysis and Reporting**

**Draft Evaluation Report**

Comprehensive analysis of contribution claims, tiered capacity trajectories, process tracing tests, and policy influence maps.

15 days

**Final**

**Final Report Deliverable Package**

Integrated Final Evaluation Report; cleaned anonymized datasets & codebooks; completed Outcome Register; standalone **Policy & Programme Influence Map**; and a **3-page plain-language Learning Brief**.

20 days

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The Endline Evaluation will be conducted over a period of **60 days.**

Payment tranches are strictly tied to formal technical approval of deliverables by the ReDSS MEAL Unit :

- **Tranche 1 (15%):** Upon formal clearance of the Inception Report & Tools (Deliverable 1).
- **Tranche 2 (25%):** Upon submission and technical review of Raw Data, Field Report, and Clean Datasets (Deliverable 2).
- **Tranche 3 (60%) :** Upon final clearance and sign-off of the Integrated Final Report, Policy Influence Map, and 3-page Learning Brief (Deliverable 4).

## Proposed Composition of Team

ReDSS accepts applications from qualified firms, registered consortiums, or partnerships. The bidding entity must demonstrate expertise in **Theory-Based Evaluations (TBE)**, Process Tracing, Outcome Harvesting, and qualitative research in displacement contexts across Kenya. The team must fulfill the following key roles:

- **Lead Evaluator / MEAL Specialist :** Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Evaluation, Development Studies, Economics, or Social Sciences. Minimum 10 years of experience leading complex evaluations in humanitarian/development sectors. Documented expertise in Contribution Analysis, Process Tracing, and reconstructing capacity baselines without non-treatment comparison groups.
- **Qualitative & Policy Specialist :** Advanced degree in Public Policy, Political Science, or International Relations. Documented expertise in Outcome Harvesting, Process Tracing, and conducting high-level KIIs with senior government officials (e.g., DRS, Shirika Plan Secretariat, County Executives in Garissa/Turkana) and bilateral donors.
- **Research Uptake & Document Audit Specialist :** Expertise in policy analysis, bibliometrics, and grey literature auditing within international development. Proven ability to map policy influence pathways and produce clear visual data products (Policy & Programme Influence Maps).
- **Research Associates (Refugee & Community Researchers) :** Minimum 3 years of experience in social research. Bidders **must** meaningfully include researchers with lived experience of displacement (drawn from Kakuma, Dadaab, or Nairobi) as core evaluators and co-facilitators. Must demonstrate prior training in research ethics, safeguarding, and Do No Harm principles.

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

The desired qualifications for the firm/consortiums, partnerships of individuals are:

- Advanced degrees in Statistics, Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Economics, Social Sciences, or related fields; with extensive experience in research and data management.
- Should have at least 5 years’ experience in conducting end-line surveys/evaluations, with a proven track record related to assessment of Research-based or evidence generation projects.
- At least 5 years of proven Experience conducting baseline Evaluations for projects with no registered baseline data.
- At least 5 years of proven experience with Theory-Based Evaluations, Outcome harvesting and contribution analysis.
- A deep thematic understanding of the Displacement Contexts in Kenya, **Refugees Act (2021)** and the **Shirika Plan**.
- Proven ability to deliver high-quality, "utilization-focused" reports within strict timelines.
- The evaluation team should demonstrate meaningful inclusion of researchers with lived experience of displacement, either as research associates, advisors, or core team members.
- Experience with evaluations commissioned by bilateral donors, including Kingdom of the Netherlands (DGIS) -funded programmes, is an added advantage.
- Excellent data analysis, presentation, and visualization skills.
- If a firm, should be registered under the Laws of Kenya.

## Technical supervision

The selected consultant will work under the supervision of:

- *ReDSS Kenya Manager.*
- *ReDSS Kenya Learning Specialist.*

## Location and support

Submissions for this consultancy are open to bids for firms with team members based in Kenya. Ideally the (lead) consultant and the team members will be based in Kenya.

The Consultant(s) will provide her/his/their own computer and mobile telephone.

What ReDSS will provide access to:

1. Evidence and knowledge products that have been produced by the Kenya evidence Platform (KEP) in the past 3 years and the affiliated Forced Migration and Research Network in Kenya (FOMREK).
2. Participants database for KEP activities over the years by all the 3 partners.
3. Indicators Performance tracking Table and the Log Frame and Theory of Change (TOC).
4. Annual Reports submitted to the donor for Year 1 and 2 and any activity-specific reports needed.
5. Policy Makers, Academics and other Stakeholders Mapped by the consultants; ReDSS will support access to these actors.

### Travel

The Consultant will be expected to arrange for his/her own transportation, meals, and accommodation in the field areas (Nairobi, Kakuma, Dadaab) for data collection should the presented methodology demand so. The consultant is also expected to make adequate provisions for this in the Financial Proposal.

### TERMS & CONDITIONS

DRC will evaluate proposals and award the assignment based on technical and financial feasibility in line with DRC Procurement guidelines. DRC reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal received without disclosing reasons to applicants and is not bound to accept the lowest bidder.

### CONFIDENTIALITY & INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

All information presented, obtained, and produced is to be treated as DRC’s property and is considered confidential for all other purposes than what is outlined in these terms of reference.

All materials, transcripts, reports, and digital assets developed under this consultancy will remain the sole property of DRC/ReDSS. The firm will hand over all editable files, documentation, data sets and report Upon completion.

title: Oficial Shelter - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a **Oficial Shelter** altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a DRC está buscando un/a **Oficial Shelter** será responsable de liderar y ejecutar acciones de recuperación temprana en los sectores de Shelter e Infraestructura.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de Equipo de Shelter y el acompañamiento técnico del Especialista Nacional de WASH, Shelter & Infraestructura, el Oficial de Shelter será responsable de liderar y ejecutar acciones de recuperación temprana en los sectores de Shelter e Infraestructura. Asegurará la ejecución oportuna y de calidad de las actividades de evaluaciones de necesidades, distribuciones de insumos y mejoras de infraestructura comunitaria e institucional afectada por la emergencia. Asimismo, apoyará la coordinación con autoridades, líderes comunitarios y otros actores humanitarios para garantizar una respuesta integrada, centrada en la protección y alineada con los estándares humanitarios aplicables.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Evaluaciones**

- Realizar evaluaciones rápidas multisectoriales y sectoriales para identificar necesidades de alojamiento e infraestructura en contextos de recuperación temprana.
- Realizar la identificación de viviendas que hayan recibido la inspección de daños por los organismos competentes y que requieran reparaciones ligeras y medias.
- Realizar la identificación de las infraestructuras comunitarias (como escuelas, centros de salud, u otros espacios que presten servicios esenciales), que hayan sido afectadas por la emergencia y que requieran reparaciones no estructurales.
- Completar los diagnósticos técnicos para las obras de rehabilitaciones de infraestructuras comunitarias y reparaciones ligeras y medias de viviendas.
- Apoyar la identificación y selección de comunidades y hogares beneficiarios que requieran apoyo con asistencia de NFIs.
- Identificar, analizar y escalar oportunamente necesidades críticas, riesgos emergentes, brechas de asistencia y desafíos operacionales que requieran decisiones inmediatas o movilización adicional de recursos.

**Implementación**

- Planificar, ejecutar y documentar la distribución de artículos no alimentarios (NFI) relacionados con alojamiento, garantizando la calidad, trazabilidad y rendición de cuentas del proceso.
- Elaborar especificaciones técnicas, estimaciones de cantidades de obra y planes de trabajo para la contratación de servicios de rehabilitación de infraestructuras comunitarias esenciales.
- Supervisar obras de rehabilitación de infraestructuras comunitarias.
- Preparar las especificaciones técnicas para la compra de materiales y kits de reparación.
- Elaborar las especificaciones técnicas para los trabajos de reparaciones ligeras y medianas de viviendas; lo que implica la definición de kits de reparación o la documentación necesaria para la contratación del servicio por contratistas.
- Brindar capacitación técnica a las familias asistidas sobre técnicas de reparación segura, incorporando elementos de reducción de riesgos de desastres.
- Monitorear la calidad técnica de las obras ejecutadas por contratistas
- Realizar el seguimiento del avance físico de las actividades y verificar el cumplimiento de estándares técnicos, de calidad, seguridad, protección y gestión ambiental, preparando los informes técnicos correspondientes y los documentos administrativos necesarios para los pagos y cierres de contratos.

**Registros**

- Documentar de manera continua resultados operacionales, desafíos, brechas y lecciones identificadas para apoyar la adaptación rápida de la respuesta y la planificación de la recuperación temprana.
- Garantizar la correcta recopilación, almacenamiento y protección de los datos de las personas beneficiarias y demás información requerida para el reporte de actividades e indicadores de los proyectos.

**Coordinación y enlace**

- Cuando sea requerido participar en los mecanismos de coordinación humanitaria a nivel nacional, regional y local, incluyendo Grupos Sectoriales/Clusters u otros espacios relevantes, compartiendo información sobre necesidades, brechas, avances y prioridades de intervención.
- Cuando sea requerido coordinar con autoridades competentes, organizaciones humanitarias y actores comunitarios para evitar duplicaciones, promover complementariedades y asegurar una respuesta oportuna e integrada.
- Participar en los espacios de coordinación dentro de DRC con los equipos de otros sectores programáticos como EcRec y Protección, para garantizar la implementación integrada con una planificación adecuada de las actividades.

**Transversales**

- Representar a la organización de manera profesional y ética en todas las actividades realizadas, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos, la adecuada gestión de la información y la seguridad de la documentación del proyecto.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el especialista WASI.
- Realizar las actividades de campo conforme a los procedimientos de seguridad, acceso humanitario y gestión de riesgos de la organización, reportando oportunamente incidentes, restricciones y cambios en el contexto operacional.
- Garantizar que todas las actividades incorporen los enfoques de protección, inclusión, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP), prevención de la explotación y abuso sexual (PSEA) y participación comunitaria.

**Experiencia y competencias técnicas:**

- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia en la implementación de programas humanitarios de Shelter y/o infraestructura comunitaria.
- Conocimiento de los estándares nacionales y humanitarios aplicables al sector.
- Experiencia en supervisión de obras, contratistas y actividades de construcción o rehabilitación.
- Buen manejo de normas, estándares y prácticas sobre obras de construcción.
- Título universitario en Ingeniería Civil o Arquitectura. Se valorará experiencia demostrable en programas humanitarios de WASH, Shelter e Infraestructura.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas (Microsoft Office) y experiencia en recolección y gestión de datos mediante plataformas digitales como Kobo Toolbox o similares.
- Capacidad de coordinación con autoridades locales, organizaciones humanitarias y líderes comunitarios.
- Habilidad para trabajar en zonas remotas y realizar visitas frecuentes a terreno.
- Compromiso con los principios humanitarios, la rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP) y la política de salvaguarda/protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA).
- Capacidad de adaptarse a situaciones cambiantes según sea necesario.
- Capacidad de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.

[*Deseable*](https://reliefweb.int/javascript:void(0))

- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Conocimiento de principios y enfoques de Protección en la acción humanitaria;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad para fomentar un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y mantener relaciones efectivas con socios implementadores y actores locales;
- Conocimiento del marco legal venezolano aplicable y de los principios del derecho internacional humanitario y de los derechos humanos.

**Educación:**

- Título en Ingeniería Civil/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente, con experiencia en WASH y Shelter o Infraestructura.

**Idioma:**

- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 4 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Viernes 20 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Noviembre 2026

title: Consultoría especialista de medios de vida pecuarios y pesqueros para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Aco
body:
DRC Venezuela busca una persona Consultor(a) en Medios de Vida Pecuarios y Pesqueros que pueda brindar asistencia técnica especializada a hogares dedicados a la producción pecuaria de traspatio y la pesca artesanal para fortalecer la protección y resiliencia de sus medios de vida frente a los impactos asociados al fenómeno de El Niño.

**1. Antecedentes**

El Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una organización humanitaria internacional que trabaja en más de 40 países. Brinda protección y asistencia a personas refugiadas, desplazadas internas, retornadas, migrantes y comunidades de acogida, siguiendo los principios humanitarios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

DRC Venezuela opera desde Caracas y cinco bases: Maracaibo, Guasdualito, Carúpano, Sur del Lago y La Guaira. En el estado Sucre, DRC implementa acciones orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de las comunidades frente a los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño y los períodos prolongados de sequía. En los municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez, las comunidades han reportado una disminución de las precipitaciones, aumento de las temperaturas y afectaciones sobre la disponibilidad de agua, con impactos directos en la producción agrícola, la pesca artesanal y los ingresos de los hogares. Asimismo, se identifican pérdidas productivas recurrentes y una creciente presión sobre los medios de vida que sostienen la seguridad alimentaria de las familias.

En respuesta a este contexto, DRC implementará acciones anticipatorias para proteger los medios de vida agrícolas y pesqueros mediante la entrega de insumos productivos, asistencia técnica y fortalecimiento de capacidades que permitan reducir las pérdidas asociadas a la sequía y mantener la continuidad de las actividades productivas. Para ello, se requiere la contratación de un(a) Consultor(a) en Medios de Vida Pecuarios y Pesqueros, responsable de brindar acompañamiento técnico especializado, desarrollar procesos formativos y apoyar la implementación y seguimiento de las actividades previstas por el proyecto.

**2. Objetivos**

**Objetivo general:**

Fortalecer la resiliencia y la capacidad de protección de los medios de vida de hogares dedicados a la pesca artesanal y la cría de animales de traspatio en los municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez, mediante procesos de identificación técnica, formación, asistencia especializada y acceso a insumos productivos que contribuyan a reducir las pérdidas ocasionadas por la sequía y los efectos asociados al fenómeno de El Niño.

**Objetivos específicos:**

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios de los componentes pesquero y pecuario**, mediante diagnósticos de campo que permitan identificar las condiciones productivas, necesidades, capacidades y vulnerabilidades de los hogares, de acuerdo con los criterios establecidos por DRC.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación para la protección de los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a los efectos de la sequía**, abordando temas relacionados con la gestión sostenible del recurso pesquero, buenas prácticas de pesca artesanal, manejo y conservación de equipos e insumos, así como prácticas de alimentación, sanidad, bioseguridad y manejo de animales de traspatio en contextos de escasez hídrica.
3. **Brindar asistencia técnica para la identificación de necesidades productivas y la definición de los kits e insumos más adecuados para cada hogar participante,** así como acompañar su uso e implementación con el fin de fortalecer y proteger los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a los efectos de la sequía y el fenómeno de El Niño.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**, que documente la implementación de las actividades, los principales logros alcanzados, las mejoras observadas en las capacidades productivas y de resiliencia de los hogares participantes, y las recomendaciones para fortalecer la protección de los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a futuras amenazas climáticas.

**3. Alcance del trabajo**

La consultoría cubre los siguientes componentes:

**Objetivo específico**

1. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios de los componentes pesquero y pecuario
2. Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación para la protección de los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a los efectos de la sequía
3. Brindar asistencia técnica para la identificación de necesidades productivas y la definición de los kits e insumos más adecuados para cada hogar participante
4. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados

**Metas**

1. Evaluar al menos a 100 hogares pesqueros, para seleccionar 90 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base)
2. Evaluar al menos a 40 hogares con cría de animales traspatio, para seleccionar 30 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base)
3. Diseñar un programa formativo para medios de vida pesqueros, de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo.
4. Impartir talleres de formación dirigidas a pescadores organizados en al menos tres grupos de 30 participantes cada uno, para un total de 90 personas capacitadas.
5. Diseñar un programa formativo para cría de animales traspatio, de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo.
6. Impartir talleres de formación dirigida a 30 pequeños productores, para un total de 30 personas capacitadas.
7. Definir kits personalizados de acuerdo a la necesidad de cada participante, para 60 pescadores y 30 personas con cría de animales traspatio.
8. Acompañar en la entrega de los kits en caso de requerir explicar detalles técnicos del uso de determinados equipos entregados.
9. Aplicar una línea de salida a los participantes (92 encuestas)
10. Elaborar 1 informe técnico de resultados

**Zonas de implementación**

- Comunidades de los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez
- Comunidades de los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar la formación
- Comunidades de los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar las entregas.
- Comunidades de los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Valdez: Espacio para realizar línea de salida puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes

**Nota:** la persona consultora no tendrá que cubrir los costos de traslados a las comunidades ni la adquisición de materiales formativos, toda vez que serán cubiertos por DRC.

**4. Productos esperados**

Los productos se entregan de forma progresiva durante el contrato, según las prioridades que fije el Líder de recuperación económica con el Gerente de base. Los plazos y productos son indicativos y se cuentan desde la firma del contrato.

**Producto**

1. Diagnóstico inicial, plan de trabajo detallado y fichas técnicas definitivas de los kits de pesca y kits pecuarios - **Plazo indicativo:** Semana 2.
2. Informe de evaluación diagnóstica y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario y pesquero - **Plazo indicativo:** Semanas 3-5
3. Diseñar dos programas de formación para la protección de los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a los efectos de la sequía - **Plazo indicativo:** Semanas 5-6
4. Informe de facilitación de dos programas de formación para la protección de los medios de vida pesqueros y pecuarios frente a los efectos de la sequía - **Plazo indicativo:** Semanas 7-11
5. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados - **Plazo indicativo:** Semanas 12-14

Cada mes la persona consultora entrega, junto con su factura, un timesheet con las horas trabajadas por componente y un breve reporte de avance.

**5. Dedicación, modalidad y supervisión**

- **Período:** desde la firma del contrato, prevista para noviembre de 2026, hasta febrero de 2027. Puede extenderse por enmienda según necesidades y presupuesto.
- **Dedicación:** por horas, según las necesidades del programa. El total no puede superar **640 horas**, DRC no garantiza un mínimo de horas.
- **Modalidad:** Presencial. El consultor deberá trasladarse con el equipo de DRC a las comunidades de intervención del proyecto, en el cronograma acordado con la oficina de la base de DRC.
- **Supervisión:** La coordinación diaria es con el Gerente de Recuperación Económica. También habrá coordinación con Supply cuando aplique.
- **Recursos que aporta DRC:** acceso a la documentación interna necesaria, costos de traslado a comunidades y material didáctico requerido. La persona consultora usa su propio equipo y conexión, así como la propiedad intelectual del desarrollo de las formaciones.

**6. Perfil requerido**

**Requisitos obligatorios**

- Profesional universitario en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería en Producción Animal, Ingeniería Agropecuaria, Ingeniería Pesquera, Biología o carreras afines relacionadas con los sectores pecuario, pesquero y el fortalecimiento de medios de vida rurales.
- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional comprobable en el diseño, implementación o acompañamiento de proyectos vinculados a la producción pecuaria, pesca artesanal, extensión rural o fortalecimiento de medios de vida agropecuarios y pesqueros.
- Experiencia en la realización de diagnósticos productivos y caracterización de beneficiarios, incluyendo la identificación de necesidades, capacidades y oportunidades de fortalecimiento de medios de vida rurales.
- Experiencia en el desarrollo e implementación de procesos de formación, asistencia técnica y acompañamiento productivo dirigidos a productores agropecuarios, pescadores artesanales, organizaciones comunitarias o promotores locales.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en enfoques de adaptación al cambio climático y gestión de riesgos en sistemas productivos agropecuarios, incluyendo medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de los medios de vida rurales frente a eventos climáticos extremos.
- Experiencia de trabajo de campo con comunidades rurales, poblaciones vulnerables, personas desplazadas, migrantes, refugiadas y/o comunidades de acogida.
- Capacidad demostrada para facilitar procesos participativos, relacionarse con diversos actores comunitarios e institucionales, coordinar actividades en terreno y trabajar de manera efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Habilidades para la elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de resultados y presentación de recomendaciones derivadas de procesos de diagnóstico, capacitación y asistencia técnica.
- Disponibilidad para iniciar en noviembre de 2026 y trasladarse a las comunidades de los municipios indicados, de preferencia en horarios de la mañana.

**Requisitos deseables**

- Experiencia previa de trabajo con organizaciones humanitarias, agencias de cooperación internacional o programas de recuperación temprana y resiliencia.
- Conocimiento de los sistemas productivos pecuarios, pesqueros y de subsistencia predominantes en el estado Sucre u otras zonas rurales y costeras de Venezuela.

**7. Contenido y presentación de la oferta**

Las ofertas deben incluir:

1. **CV** de la persona consultora, con tres referencias profesionales verificables.
2. Propuesta de los dos contenidos formativos (preliminar) de cada programa: de cría de animales traspatio, y pesquero, detallando la siguiente información:

**Número de módulo / Nombre de la sesión / Contenido a abordar propuesto / Horas requeridas / Material didáctico requerido**

1

2

3

4

**Total horas:**

3.**Oferta financiera:** tarifa diaria en USD, **todo incluido** (honorarios, impuestos, equipo, conexión y cualquier otro costo), por una jornada de 8 horas. La tarifa horaria se calcula como la tarifa diaria dividida entre 8.

4.**Documentos administrativos:** RIF vigente, documento de identidad o registro mercantil, y formulario de registro de proveedor de DRC.

5.Declaración firmada de ausencia de conflicto de interés y aceptación del Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC.

No se solicita propuesta técnica.

Las ofertas se envían a rfq.ven@drc.ngo antes del 25/11/2026 indicando en el asunto la referencia **Consultoría Medíos de Vida Sucre**. Las preguntas se reciben hasta 20/11/2026 y las respuestas se comparten con todos los oferentes. Las ofertas recibidas fuera de plazo no serán consideradas.

**8. Criterios de evaluación**

Las ofertas que cumplan los requisitos administrativos y obligatorios se evalúan con una ponderación de 70 % técnica y 30 % financiera. La evaluación técnica se basa en el CV y las referencias. Solo pasan a la evaluación financiera las ofertas con al menos 49 de 70 puntos técnicos. DRC puede entrevistar a las personas mejor puntuadas.

**Criterio**

- Formación académica en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería de Producción Animal, Ingeniería Pesquera, Ingeniería Agropecuaria, Biología o áreas afines - **20 Puntos**
- Experiencia demostrable en proyectos de producción pecuaria y pesca artesanal, incluyendo el fortalecimiento de medios de vida rurales, la asistencia técnica a productores y pescadores, y la implementación de estrategias de resiliencia, adaptación al cambio climático y gestión del riesgo frente a eventos climáticos extremos - **20 Puntos**
- Experiencia demostrable en diagnósticos productivos, selección de beneficiarios, capacitación y asistencia técnica a productores agropecuarios y pescadores artesanales - **15 Puntos**
- Calidad de la propuesta metodológica para la ejecución de la consultoría - **15 Puntos**

**Total técnico: 70 Puntos**

Oferta financiera: tarifa diaria más baja / tarifa evaluada × 30 - 30 **Puntos**

**Total: 100 Puntos**

**9. Condiciones contractuales**

- **Contrato:** Contrato de Servicios de Consultoría de DRC, con las Condiciones Generales de Contrato y el Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC como anexos obligatorios.
- **Pagos:** mensuales, por transferencia, según las horas efectivamente trabajadas, a la tarifa horaria derivada de la tarifa diaria ofertada. Cada pago requiere factura válida y timesheet aprobado por el Gerente de base. Se aplican las retenciones de ley. El monto total no puede superar el equivalente a 640 horas.
- **Confidencialidad:** toda la información de DRC, de sus donantes, de su personal y de las personas participantes es confidencial. Los productos de la consultoría son propiedad de DRC.
- **Protección de datos:** el tratamiento de datos personales, incluidos los de personas beneficiarias, sigue las políticas de protección de datos de DRC.
- **Conducta:** la persona consultora firma y cumple el Código de Conducta de DRC, incluida la tolerancia cero frente a la explotación y el abuso sexual, el fraude y la corrupción.
- **Conflicto de interés:** no pueden participar personas de DRC Venezuela ni que tengan vínculos con personal involucrado en esta contratación.
- **Derecho de DRC:** DRC puede aceptar o rechazar cualquier oferta, total o parcialmente, sin obligación de justificar su decisión.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist assists newly arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake, assessment and provide program orientation to clients eligible for employment services.
- Provide job readiness training and job search coaching and connect clients with job opportunities.
