title: Nutrition Specialist
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**IRC Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. IRC reaches over 50,000 clients annually across the US through programs for resettled refugees, asylum seekers, unaccompanied children, survivors of torture and trafficking, and individuals from local communities welcoming newcomers.

**Scope of work:**

The Nutrition Specialist supports the Health Promotion Programs team within the New Roots Program by leading the weekly food security work, including the food distribution, and by connecting that work to New Roots Garden production. This role runs the weekly distribution, supports spring and summer garden production that supplies the food distribution projects, and creates opportunities for clients to take part in the garden. The position also focuses on data collection and entry for these projects and on monthly and quarterly reporting, in partnership with the Health Promotion Coordinator and the Safety, Health and Education Programs Manager.

**Essential Responsibilities:**

- Run all aspects of the weekly food security program and food distribution, including planning, setup, participant check-in, distribution, and cleanup
- Receive, store, and handle food safely, and keep inventory and supplies organized
- Support spring and summer New Roots Garden production to supply the food distribution projects
- Create opportunities for clients to visit and take part in the New Roots Garden, and help them feel welcome and comfortable on site
- Collect and enter data for the food security and garden projects accurately and on time, keeping participant information confidential
- Prepare monthly and quarterly reports in partnership with the Health Promotion Coordinator and the Safety, Health and Education Programs Manager
- Promote a welcoming, inclusive, and culturally responsive environment at distribution and garden sites
- Support Health Promotion activities as needed and as available

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Health Promotion Coordinator  
**Position directly supervises:** Volunteers and interns under the project  
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** All IRC internal partners, Northwest Harvest, 2nd Harvest, Spokane Libraries and Growing Neighbors.

**Job Requirements:**

- Experience with food distribution, food security, nutrition, or community health programs, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
- Experience with data collection and data entry, and comfort with spreadsheets or databases
- Attention to detail and ability to keep accurate, confidential records
- Experience working with diverse populations
- Strong communication and organizational skills
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team and across multiple sites
- Food handler card or willingness to obtain one, if required
- \[Ability to lift 80 lbs. and work outdoors in the garden, with or without reasonable accommodation, if these are essential job functions.
- (Preferred) Previous agricultural or urban gardening experience
- (Preferred) Bilingual candidates
- (Preferred) Lived experience with food insecurity or connection to the communities we serve

**Working Environment:**

- Standard, professional office environment combined with community-based work, including weekly food distribution and outdoor garden work. \[Remote or hybrid details, if any.\]

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23-$25/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer the following benefits to short term employees in the US: 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, sick leave, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Human Capability Transformation ‎Advisor
source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
body:
**Organizational context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) is implementing a comprehensive institutional transformation agenda under the URCS Strategy 2026-2030 and the Institutional Capabilities Programme. As part of this transformation, URCS intends to evolve its current Human Resources Department into a strategic Human Capability Function, moving beyond traditional HR administration towards a model that enables workforce capability, leadership development, talent management, organizational culture, employee and volunteer experience, succession planning, and organizational effectiveness.

To support this transition, URCS has invited technical assistance from IFRC through the recruitment and deployment of an experienced HR professional. The position will be recruited and contracted by IFRC and seconded to URCS for an extended period to provide dedicated technical leadership and implementation support throughout the transformation process.

The role is intended to serve as a trusted advisor and technical expert, working alongside a newly hired HR Director and URCS leadership to design, guide and support the implementation of the Human Capability Transformation Programme that focuses on strengthening workforce planning, talent and leadership development, organizational culture, performance management, employee and volunteer experience, people analytics and digital people systems. Through institutional capacity building, change management and knowledge transfer, the Programme aims to create a resilient, high-performing and future-ready organization capable of delivering its humanitarian mission and strategic objectives through 2030 and beyond.

The position is intended as seconded technical backstop supporting both strategic development and practical implementation of the transition.

**Job purpose**

The Human Capability Transformation Advisor will serve as a trusted technical expert and change leader, supporting URCS in the design and institutionalization of a comprehensive Human Capability Transformation Programme aligned with the URCS Strategy 2026–2030 and the Institutional Capabilities Development Programme.

The Advisor will support the transition of the traditional Human Resources function into a modern, strategic Human Capability function that strengthens organizational performance, leadership, workforce sustainability and effectiveness. This will include strategic workforce planning, talent and performance management, leadership and capability development, organizational culture, succession planning, and employee and volunteer experience.

Working closely with the Deputy Director General Organization and Human Capability Development, HR Director and other key stakeholders, the role holder will provide strategic advice and hands-on implementation support to strengthen operating models, systems, governance and ways of working. A key focus will be coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer to build internal capability and ensure that new approaches are effectively embedded and can be sustained and continuously developed by URCS.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

**Strategic Human Capability Transformation**

- Provide strategic leadership and technical advice for the implementation of the Human Capability Programme.
- Support the establishment of the future Human Capability operating model, ensuring alignment with the URCS Strategy 2026-2030 and Institutional Capabilities (NSD) Programme.
- Introduce and embed good international practices, systems and methodologies that strengthen organizational capability and workforce effectiveness.

**Organizational Development and Effectiveness**

- Strengthen organizational effectiveness through improved organizational design, workforce structures and capability management.
- Support the identification and closure of critical organizational capability gaps and succession risks.
- Promote accountability, organizational resilience and effective people management practices across the URCS.

**Strategic Workforce Planning**

- Establish strategic workforce planning processes that align people capabilities with current and future organizational needs.
- Strengthen workforce analysis, capability mapping and succession planning to support sustainable organizational growth.

**Leadership Development and Talent Management**

- Support the development of a leadership system that strengthens leadership capability at all levels of the organization.
- Establish sustainable approaches to talent management, leadership development and succession planning.
- Coach and mentor leaders in people management, organizational effectiveness and change leadership.

**Learning and Organizational Capability Development**

- Support the establishment of an integrated learning and capability development system aligned with organizational priorities.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing and professional development across URCS.

**Performance Management and Rewards**

- Support the development of performance management and reward systems that promote accountability, engagement and high performance.
- Strengthen the use of performance data to inform talent, workforce and organizational decisions.

**Organizational Culture and Employee Experience**

- Support the development of a unified organizational culture aligned with URCS values and strategic objectives.
- Strengthening employee engagement, wellbeing and employee experience practices to improve retention and organizational commitment.

**HR Business Partner Capability Development**

- Establish the HR Business Partner model as a strategic partner to managers and leaders across URCS.
- Strengthen the advisory, workforce planning and organizational development capabilities of Human Capability staff.

**People Analytics and Digital Human Capability Systems**

- Promote data-driven decision-making through workforce analytics, people metrics and management reporting.
- Support the development of digital systems and tools that improve workforce management and organizational effectiveness.

**Change Management and Transformation Support**

- Lead and support change management efforts that enable the successful adoption of new systems, structures and ways of working.
- Strengthen stakeholder engagement, organizational readiness and leadership alignment throughout the transformation process.

**Capacity Strengthening and Knowledge Transfer**

- Act as a strategic adviser and mentor to the HR Director and Human Capability Programme leadership team that is managed by the HR Director.
- Build sustainable institutional capability through coaching, knowledge transfer and implementation support.

Ensure the long-term sustainability of the transformation through structured handover and institutionalization of systems and practice

Duties applicable to all staff  
‎1.‎ Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals. ‎  
‎2.‎ Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.‎  
‎3.‎ Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.‎

**Education**

- Advanced university degree/ postgraduate qualification in one or more of the ‎following fields: Organizational Development, Management and Leadership, Human ‎Resources Management, Human Capital Management, Organizational Psychology, ‎Business Administration (MBA), Human Capital Strategy or Change Management or ‎other relevant fields. ‎
- Professional certifications in HR and organizational development/change management ‎would be considered an asset

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in senior HR, ‎Human Capital, Organizational Development or Human Capability leadership roles.‎
- Demonstrated experience leading large-scale HR transformation or organizational ‎transformation programmes, including organizational development, change ‎management and culture transformation. ‎
- Experience developing and implementing workforce planning, talent management, ‎succession, performance and leadership/capability development systems.‎
- Proven experience providing strategic advice to executive leadership and leading ‎capacity strengthening, institutional development and knowledge transfer initiatives.‎
- Experience working in humanitarian, international development, NGO or public sector ‎environments, including organizations operating through decentralized networks and ‎branch structures.‎
- Experience working in complex emergencies, recovery or transition contexts; previous ‎experience within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is an asset.‎

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Strong knowledge and practical experience in: Human Capability Strategy, HR ‎Transformation, Organizational Development and Organizational Design
- Knowledge and experience in Workforce Planning, Leadership Development, Talent ‎Management and Succession Planning
- Strong programme/project management skills, with the ability to translate ‎transformation strategies and roadmaps into prioritized, practical and measurable ‎implementation plans.‎
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to build ‎alignment and drive organizational change across diverse functions and seniority ‎levels.‎
- Experience and knowledge of Learning and Development processes, Performance ‎Management, Managing Employee Experience and Enriching Organizational Culture. ‎
- Knowledge and experience in executing Change Management, Conducting People ‎Analytics
- Knowledge and experience of HRIS and Digital HR Systems ‎
- Proven experience in Coaching and Mentoring Facilitation and Capacity Development
- Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic ‎digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem ‎solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.‎
- Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values. ‎
- Fluent spoken and written English

**Values:** Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability  
**Core competencies:** Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society ‎and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

title: Protection Officer
body:
**Job Title:** Protection Officer

**Function**: Programme Implementation

**Job Group**: Programme

**Duty Station**: Ukraine (Kherson)

**Administrative Line Manager**: Team Leader

**Technical Line Manager:** Team Leader

**Position Type**: Full-time

**ABOUT US**

NP (Nonviolent Peaceforce) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022, documenting civilian protection challenges, providing protection advocacy, and engaging with a variety of local and international stakeholders and responding to identified civilian protection needs. NP has a holistic and forward leaning approach to civilian protection in Ukraine with a particular focus on increasing the safety and security of civilians, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), as they move across the country, with a focus on population groups exposed to vulnerabilities.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The role of the Protection Officer (PO) is to support the implementation of civilian protection and violence-prevention programming for those affected by conflict.

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Project implementation**

- Provide support for the day-to-day implementation of project activities in accordance with the agreed work plans and log-frames.
- Support and assist the Team Leader (TL) in the engagement and relationship building with relevant stakeholders, including local humanitarian NGOs, community-based organizations, and local authorities.
- Support in identifying protection needs in Kherson by conducting site assessments, context monitoring, and community outreach
- Conduct and facilitate community meetings and dialogues in the project areas.
- Support and assist the TL and team in conducting and facilitating training and seminars for community and project partners, for example, Civilian Protection – Early Warning and Early Response (CP-EWER), International Humanitarian Law (IHL), Human Rights Law (HRL), Child Protection (CP), Gender Based Violence (GBV).
- Support in providing protective accompaniment to civilians exposed to vulnerabilities, particularly the elderly and people with special needs.
- Support and assist, monitor, verify and report incidents of violence and civilian displacement.
- Regularly monitor provision and the availability of humanitarian services to civilians in need, conduct referrals, when necessary.
- Write and submit activity reports documenting the completion of protection activities and their impact.

**Duties Applicable to All Staff**

- Actively work towards the achievement of the goals and mandate of NP.
- Abide by and work in accordance with NP values and principles as provided in the Global Employee Handbook and existing policies.
- Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education**

*Required*

- University degree in a related field (Social Science, Development Studies, etc.).
- Interest in peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and civilian protection and human rights. Practical experience in these fields is highly desirable.

*Preferred*

- Qualifications or commensurate practical experience in peacebuilding, conflict transformation or nonviolent peacekeeping.

**Work Experience**

*Required*

- 1-2 years relevant work experience in civilian/humanitarian/child protection and human rights.

*Preferred*

- NGO/ humanitarian work.
- Post-conflict/conflict area experience.
- Experience in community organizing/mobilization.
- Experience leading or coordinating trainings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

*Required*

- Understanding on civil protection and human rights frameworks
- Understanding of conflict dynamics in Ukraine
- Understanding of the humanitarian and **DO NO HARM** principles
- Knowledge and understanding in peace making, peacekeeping and peace building and social cohesion concepts
- Report writing skills
- Able to communicate in oral and written English, as well as Ukrainian and/or Russian

title: Protection from Violence Manager Ethiopia North Afar
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you passionate about advancing protection and making a tangible difference in the lives of people affected by violence and displacement?

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a **Protection from Violence (PfV) Project Manager** to lead its project portfolio in the North Area Office. This is an opportunity to provide strategic and operational leadership, drive high-quality protection programming, strengthen accountability and ensure effective project delivery in line with NRC standards, strategies and donor requirements.

As NRC continues to strengthen and expand its PfV programming across Ethiopia, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering integrated protection interventions across Amhara, Afar and Wolkait Tegede Setit Humera, while contributing to the wider programme's ambitions across the country.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Female candidates are encouraged to apply.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your specific responsibilities:

- Train, mentor and coach staff delivering specialised protection services, including protection case management and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), in line with NRC modalities, tools and guidance.
- Promote consistency and alignment of specialised protection activities across field teams and support the development or adaptation of common guidelines, tools and standard operating procedures (SOPs) where required.
- Ensure that tools and SOPs align with NRC approaches to specialised protection services and that appropriate transition or capacity-development plans are in place where needed.
- Lead or coordinate area-based, conflict-sensitive analysis and monitoring of protection risks to inform programme design, implementation and adaptation.
- Ensure that an appropriate case-management tracking system is maintained or established, with due attention to confidentiality, informed consent and data protection.
- Monitor trends in protection risks emerging from specialised protection services and engage with NRC teams and other protection actors to address risks at community level.
- Coordinate with the Monitoring and Evaluation team to ensure appropriate monitoring approaches and tools and promote safe monitoring of specialised protection activities.
- Capture and share lessons learned on project methodology and implementation, and use findings to improve programme quality.
- Provide technical and managerial support for implementation of specialised protection work plans.
- Contribute to regional donor reporting, including narrative and financial inputs.
- Lead the development and design of Civilian Self-Protection (CSP) activities, ensuring that interventions are contextually appropriate and informed by protection analysis.
- Ensure that learning from CSP implementation is documented and incorporated into programme adaptation and staff development.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBZxn6Fs8NTRYp9ytigCMdvAWezj2k686m80DaIw4drkbo?e=zUcUnn) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum five years of experience in a senior project implementation or management position in a humanitarian or recovery context.
- Experience working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Technical expertise in Protection programming.
- Demonstrated results relevant to the responsibilities of the position.
- Knowledge of own leadership skills and profile.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Technical expertise and field experience in general protection case management in operation area.
- Field experience conducting case management and referrals in low-resource settings.
- Strong interpersonal skills and knowledge of the North Area operational context.
- Knowledge of local language
- Experience managing teams and working with IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Afar, Asyita.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal
body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal**

**Contracting organization**

arche nova (AN)

## 1. Introduction

arche nova (AN) ([www.arche-nova.org](http://www.arche-nova.org)), a German non-governmental organization, has since 2012, been supporting vulnerable communities in Kenya to strengthen resilience to climate change, water scarcity, food insecurity, environmental degradation, and recurrent humanitarian shocks. Working at the humanitarian-development-climate nexus, arche nova combines emergency response, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate adaptation, and sustainable development approaches to build long-term resilience and self-reliance. Together with our local partners working in Kibera; Human Needs Project (HNP) and Action for Social and Economic Progress (ASEP), we are preparing a project proposal for submission to the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The proposed intervention is envisaged for Kibera, Nairobi County, Kenya.

## 2. Background

The proposed project; “Strengthening urban resilience through a climate-smart, multifunctional satellite community hub in the Kibera slum, Nairobi, seeks to address interconnected water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), public-health, climate-resilience and community livelihood needs in Kibera. Objective: To strengthen urban resilience through WASH, income generation and social cohesion in the Kibera slum, Kenya. Target group: 20,000 people, including 55 per cent women, 35 per cent young people (18-25 years) and 10 per cent people with disability. The target groups are closely interconnected with overlapping co-benefits from the project hence a validation of the total beneficiaries reached by the project is necessary. The Junior Partner; HNP also directly benefit from the project through strengthened capacities from the senior partner ASEP.

The project components include construction of a climate-smart community hub for improved access to safe water and sanitation, livelihoods and social cohesion. Potential measures may include a solar-powered water supply, greywater treatment using nano-filtration for reuse e.g. for hydroponic farming, sanitation and bathing facilities, menstrual health and hygiene (MHM), and inclusive community engagement, a digital innovation training lab for green business, entrepreneurship, job placement, and conflict/legal advice. Building on HNP’s ‘Kibera Town Centre’, which successfully operates as a self-sustaining WASH, training and community centre. A senior-junior partnership model is being introduced: as an experienced stakeholder and AN partner, ASEP supports the smaller, locally-rooted organization HNP to facilitate better access to funding, technical support and innovation.

These are options for assessment and are not predetermined technical decisions. The project is structured around four results:

Result 1: Improved access to climate-resilient and inclusive WASH services for vulnerable residents in Kibera.

Result 2: Improved economic empowerment and green skills development for women and youth.

Result 3: Strengthened social cohesion and improved access to community justice services for underserved vulnerable community members.

Result 4: Strengthened institutional capacity and inclusive governance for sustainable service delivery.

A feasibility study is required to verify priority needs supporting the project idea to assess the suitability, affordability and sustainability of proposed measures as well as beneficiary, stakeholder and partner relationships and identify the key risks and recommend concrete adjustments to the project concept, the impact matrix and the planned measures. The study must be independent and sufficiently critical to recommend redesign, deferral or non-selection of any measure where evidence does not support it.

The study should consider applicable BMZ PT requirements and relevant OECD/DAC criteria: relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability. Cross-cutting considerations include gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights, environmental and climate safeguards, conflict sensitivity, accountability and Do No Harm.

## 3. Purpose and Scope of the Assignment

The purpose of the assignment is to provide AN and its partners with an independent, participatory and evidence-based basis for deciding on the proposed intervention and preparing a coherent, technically sound, costed and sustainable BMZ PT project proposal.

The feasibility study will:

- Validate priority needs, vulnerabilities, capacities and intended target groups in the proposed project area.
- Assess the technical, social, institutional, environmental, regulatory, operational and financial feasibility of proposed measures and compare viable alternatives.
- Analyze target groups and stakeholders, including their relationships, interests, influence, roles, coordination and potential risks of exclusion or conflict.
- Identify prerequisites, including land tenure and site access, asset ownership, water availability and rights, permits, environmental and social assessments, technical investigations, utility connections, and operation and maintenance arrangements.
- Recommend intervention logic, target groups, objectives, outputs, indicators, means of verification, assumptions and risks for the logical framework matrix; establish baseline values where feasible and propose evidence-based targets.
- Recommend sustainability, exit or transition, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) arrangements.

## 4. Methodology

The study should combine qualitative and quantitative methods and follow a participatory approach that reflects the needs and perspectives of intended beneficiaries and relevant stakeholders. The consultant shall propose a rigorous but proportionate methodology in the inception report, triangulating secondary evidence with field-based verification.

- The sampling approach must be justified, including selection of locations, respondent groups and sample size. A census or large-scale survey should not be assumed necessary unless justified by the study questions, available time and budget.
- Recent and relevant secondary data should be used wherever suitable. Sources, dates, geographic coverage and limitations must be stated; primary data collection should fill material evidence gaps rather than duplicate existing assessments.
- Data collection methods may include desk review, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, community consultations, site observations, structured facility assessments, quantitative data collection where justified, stakeholder and service mapping, risk analysis and preliminary costing.
- For every proposed outcome- and output-level indicator in the draft logical framework, assess measurability, data sources, disaggregation and feasibility of collection; establish a baseline value where evidence permits and recommend a realistic target.
- Assess the concept against the OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, explaining how each informs the feasibility judgement and recommendations.
- Data-collection tools must be shared with AN and partners for comment before fieldwork. Participation must be voluntary and informed. Personal data must be minimized, securely handled and reported in aggregated or anonymized form wherever possible.
- Validation with AN and partners should improve factual accuracy and usability but must not compromise the consultant’s independent judgement.

## 5. Tasks and Deliverables

### 5.1 Tasks

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks. The detailed methodology and sequencing will be agreed during inception.

#### Context and Initial Situation Analysis

- Review the concept note, available WASH and public-health data, relevant research, local plans and applicable national and county policies.
- Analyze Kibera’s socio-economic, public-health, environmental, climate, institutional and governance context relevant to the proposed intervention.
- Map existing and planned WASH, sanitation, MHM, livelihood and climate-resilience actors and interventions and identify synergies, referral pathways and duplication risks. Assess whether the established St. Juliet is complemented by the community service hub and or establish existing gaps.
- Verify the nature, scale and location of priority needs and identify population groups facing the greatest barriers or risks.
- Identify evidence gaps, stakeholder perceptions and assumptions requiring further investigation and prepare an evidence matrix.

1. **Stakeholder and Partner Analysis**

- Identify and engage key stakeholders, including young women, young men, parents, community and religious leaders, county and national government actors, and other civil society organisations.
- Assess the Partners regarding their roles, resources and competencies for
- project implementation.
- Evaluate the formal agreements and ownership structures between AN, ASEP, HNP
- Identify and analyse any gaps in collaboration and coordination.
- Identify synergies and confirm whether all official preconditions and authorizations for project implementation are in place

#### Needs, Target Groups and Beneficiary Analysis

- Consult residents and intended beneficiaries, including women and girls, youth, persons with disabilities, older people and other potentially marginalized groups, using safe and accessible methods.
- Suggest a beneficiary selection criterion, expected reach, affordability, barriers to access, protection concerns, participation and possible unintended consequences.
    
    **Skills Training, Employment and Income-Generation Feasibility**
- Assess the gaps and needs among intended beneficiaries for the proposed skills training, including priority skills, participation barriers, existing competencies and the extent to which the proposed training responds to local needs and market demand.
- Analyse realistic employment, self-employment and income-generation opportunities linked to the proposed skills areas, including local labour-market conditions, viable value chains, market access, competition, start-up requirements. Technical and Operational Feasibility
- Assess proposed boreholes, toilets, showers and related facilities site suitability, accessibility, privacy, safety, gender responsiveness, MHM needs, cleaning, wastewater containment and disposal, desludging, drainage and recurrent costs.
- Assess whether proposed user fees are affordable and acceptable to intended beneficiaries and determine if the expected income can adequately cover recurrent operational and maintenance costs. Environmental, Social, Regulatory and Safeguarding Analysis
- Identify risks and mitigation needs related to groundwater abstraction, wastewater, sludge, solid waste, drainage, construction, energy use and treatment residuals.
- Identify the required environmental assessment and approval pathway, permits, land-access documentation, water-resource approvals and other statutory requirements; verify status where evidence is available.
- Assess gender, disability inclusion, child and adult safeguarding, protection, community safety, affordability and equitable access.
- Identify risks of exclusion, tension, elite capture, unequal benefits, displacement or disruption of existing services, and recommend practical mitigation measures.
- Recommend proportionate community consultation, complaints and feedback mechanisms, and ethical data-protection practices.

#### Project Concept Evaluation, Design and Recommendations

- Test the theory of change and causal links between needs, activities, outputs, outcomes and intended longer-term effects.
- Assess the coherence and manageability of combining WASH, livelihoods, access to justice and institutional strengthening in one hub, and recommend whether any component should be scaled down, phased or dropped.
- Map and assess the potential legal services gaps of intended beneficiaries,availability of qualified and legally authorized legal aid providers, community justice organizations, paralegals and relevant referral services operating in Kibera.
- Review and refine the draft logical framework, including indicators, potential baselines, proposed targets where evidence permits, sources of verification, assumptions and risks.
- Recommend MEAL responsibilities, data-collection frequency, disaggregation, community feedback and learning reviews.

### 5.2 Deliverables

The consultant shall submit the following deliverables in English. Due dates will be finalized at contracting and aligned with AN’s BMZ PT proposal-development schedule.

**Inception report:** Desk-review summary and evidence gaps; refined questions; justified sampling and respondent-selection approach; stakeholder plan; fieldwork locations and schedule; ethics, safeguarding and data-management arrangements; limitations; draft tools.

**Preliminary findings briefing**: Emerging findings, evidence gaps, options, key risks and decisions requiring partner input.

**Draft feasibility study**: Context and problem analysis; needs and target groups; stakeholder and partner analysis; options appraisal; technical and operational feasibility; safeguards; OECD/DAC assessment; risks and sustainability; indicator-by-indicator review with baseline values where feasible and proposed targets.

**Project-design annexes:** Draft logical framework matrix; intervention logic/theory of change; indicators and baseline information; implementation timetable; risk register; indicative activity-based budget

**Validation and final report:** Validation session with AN and partners; final report incorporating comments; stakeholder contact list, bibliography/source list and curated, captioned photographs where appropriate and consented.

- The final report should not exceed 30 pages excluding annexes and should open with an executive summary of no more than 3 pages.
- The report must give a clear, evidence-based recommendation for each proposed measure (proceed, proceed with modifications, defer or do not proceed), with the reasons and conditions attached.
- All reports and annexes must be submitted in PDF and editable formats (MS Word and Excel) and cleaned; anonymized datasets and data-collection tools shall be submitted as annexes

## 6. Supporting Documents

AN and its partners will provide relevant available documents to support the assignment, which may include:

- The latest project concept notes, draft proposal narrative, draft logical framework/results matrix and draft budget.
- Available site information, maps and previous project report relevant to Kibera and the proposed intervention.
- Relevant BMZ PT feasibility-study guidance, templates and proposal requirements.

## 7. Skills and Experience- consultant profile

AN invites application from Kenya-based independent consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms. Where a multidisciplinary team is proposed, one team member must act as team leader and take responsibility for the quality and timely delivery of all outputs. The team should collectively demonstrate:

- Postgraduate qualification in development studies, social sciences, public health, engineering, environmental studies, economics or another relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience conducting feasibility studies, assessments or project design for development programmes in Kenya, preferably in urban informal settlements or similarly complex settings
- Experience developing institutional-donor proposals, logical frameworks, results chains, implementation plans and activity-based budgets.
- Relevant WASH and public-health expertise. Specialist engineering or water-resource conclusions must be reviewed by appropriately qualified professionals.
- Experience with participatory and mixed-methods research, stakeholder analysis and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
- Competence in gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, environmental and social risk assessment, conflict sensitivity, social cohesion and accountability.
- Strong analytical, facilitation and report-writing skills; excellent written and spoken English; willingness to conduct fieldwork in Kibera.

## 8. Work Plan and Submission

The assignment is expected to be delivered within 21 consultant working days, completed within a period agreed with AN and aligned to the proposal-development schedule. The consultant should propose a realistic allocation of days. The following distribution is indicative:

- Inception and desk review: 2–3 days.
- Fieldwork and stakeholder consultations: 5–7 days.
- Analysis and options appraisal: 4–5 days.
- Draft report and design annexes: 3–4 days.
- Validation, revisions and finalization: 2–3 days.

Fieldwork dates and submission deadlines will be agreed during inception. AN’s review periods and partner feedback must be built into the detailed workplan. Deliverables are complete only after review and acceptance by AN.

## 9. Management, Coordination, Ethics and Data Management

- The consultant reports to the designated AN focal point, who coordinates comments and confirms acceptance of deliverables.
- AN and partners will provide available project documents, facilitate introductions to stakeholders and support agreed field logistics.
- The consultant is responsible for the quality and independence of the analysis, tools, fieldwork, analysis and timely delivery. Changes to scope, fieldwork, deliverables or timeline require written agreement by AN before additional work is undertaken.
- Obtain informed consent before interviews, discussions, photographs or collection of personal information; participation must be voluntary. Use safe, accessible and culturally appropriate methods and avoid creating expectations about project approval or benefits.
- Apply safeguarding and Do No Harm principles, including appropriate protections when engaging children or other groups requiring additional safeguards.
- Protect confidentiality and securely store notes, recordings and datasets in line with the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019, and applicable research-ethics requirements. The consultant must identify any research licence, ethical clearance or other authorization required and include the time and cost in the workplan and financial proposal.
- All reports, tools, datasets, photographs commissioned under the assignment and project-design annexes shall be provided to AN and handled in accordance with the consultancy contract. The consultant may not publish confidential project information or identifiable participant data without prior written authorization. Third-party sources must be acknowledged.

## 10. Application Requirements

Applications are invited from Kenya-based individual consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms, in line with Section 7. Applications must include:

- **Cover letter** (max. 2 pages) explaining interest and suitability for the assignment, and confirming availability for the proposed period.
- **Technical proposal** (max. 10 pages) setting out understanding of the assignment and the Kibera context; proposed methodology, sampling and options-appraisal approach; work plan with allocation of days per team member and per phase; team composition and roles; quality-assurance arrangements; and ethics, safeguarding and data-protection arrangements.
- **CVs** of all proposed team members (max. 2 pages each), including at least two references from recent, similar assignments.
- **Financial proposal** in Kenya Shillings (KES), with professional fees shown as daily rate × number of days for each team member, and separate lines for field costs (e.g. enumerators, transport, venues, consultation costs), research licence or ethical-clearance costs, and applicable taxes.
- **One sample** of a feasibility study, assessment or project-design report recently completed by the lead consultant or team (or a link to it).
- **Compliance documents:** copy of KRA PIN and valid tax compliance certificate; for firms, certificate of registration or incorporation.
- **Signed declaration** of no conflict of interest.

title: Secretary General
body:
The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a new Secretary General to succeed Jan Egeland. Under his leadership, NRC has strengthened its international standing and become a prominent voice for people forced to flee. The next Secretary General will build on these achievements and lead NRC into the future.

This is an opportunity to lead one of the world's most respected humanitarian organisations, influence the international humanitarian agenda and make a real difference to people affected by conflict and displacement.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 14,000 staff work in crises across 39 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year. NRC includes the two brands NORCAP – global provider of aid expertise and solutions ([https://www.nrc.no/norcap](https://www.nrc.no/norcap)) and the displacement monitoring centre IDMC-JIPS ([https://www.internal-displacement.org/](https://www.internal-displacement.org/)).

## Responsibilities

**The opportunity:**

As Secretary General, you will lead a large and complex global organisation, set its strategic direction and ensure that NRC delivers on its humanitarian mission.

Working closely with the NRC Board and senior management group, you will be responsible for the organisation's continued development, its people and resources, and the strategic choices needed to remain effective and efficient in a changing world.

You will be NRC's leading international representative and public voice, engaging with governments, international institutions, donors and humanitarian partners. You will advocate for the rights of displaced people, influence humanitarian policy and mobilise support for NRC's work, including when this means challenging those in power.

The role requires someone who can combine a strong international presence with the ability to lead and develop a major global organisation.

## Qualifications

**The person we are looking for:**

We are seeking an accomplished international leader with strong humanitarian values, international credibility and the ability to take NRC forward.

A deep personal commitment to humanitarian principles, human dignity and the rights of people forced to flee is essential.

You bring substantial leadership experience from a complex international organisation or sector, with a track record of setting direction, making difficult decisions and leading change. You have a strong understanding of international affairs and geopolitical dynamics, and the judgement to navigate complex political and organisational challenges.

You are an effective communicator who can engage and influence senior decision-makers internationally. As a leader, you build trust, empower others and bring people together around a shared purpose.

We welcome candidates from different backgrounds who share NRC's humanitarian values and have the leadership experience and commitment needed for the role.

Your experience may come from humanitarian or international development organisations, government, diplomacy, multilateral institutions or other international sectors.

Fluency in English and proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language are required.

The position is based in Oslo, Norway, and involves substantial international travel.

**What we offer:**

- Duty Station: Oslo, Norway
- Travel: 40%
- Contract type: Permanent contract

body:
MRAPP funded by the Government of the Netherlands, aims to strengthen migration prevention efforts and improve access to migration-related information, counselling, referral and reintegration services in Iraq. The project is implemented by ICMPD in close coordination with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement and other relevant governmental and local stakeholders, with a focus on strengthening and expanding the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) model.

## Functional Overview

Working closely with the respective Migration Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator, the MRC Counsellor assists with the implementation of MRC activities and workplans, in support of effective communication, information and service delivery. They contribute to the organisation of events and outreach activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Coordinator and other Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures.

## Key Results

***Support to MRC Activities:*** Via various means and platforms such as face-to-face, phone and online, counselling, guidance, referral and information provided to a variety of clients (prospective or returning migrants, migrants, families of migrants, etc.) who visit or attend MRC activities, initiating and following up on referrals, linking them with relevant agencies depending on their needs, e.g. technical and vocational institutes to upgrade their skills or with the relevant authorities for the processing of their documents for overseas employment. Outreach activities supported via the use of media and social media and participation in online discussions, forums or symposiums, conferences, and other related events. In collaboration with the MRC Coordinator the MRC website and database, Facebook page and other social media accounts regularly updated.

***Support to Outreach Activities:*** In cooperation with relevant agencies both in the public and private sector, networks and contacts effectively established. Community events and outreach activities organised such as briefings in academic and training institutions, symposia with civil society, training of education or emigration consultancies, and the setting-up of booths, kiosks, or similar structures in public places to disseminate information and materials on safe, orderly, and regular migration, including on return and reintegration.

Knowledge materials compiled on migration that are helpful in the full operation and functioning of the MRC. Substantive contributions provided to the preparation of relevant reports, responses to client feedback and monitoring and reporting to relevant agencies on any policy or programmatic recommendations. Effective support provided to the MRC Coordinator in preparing weekly, quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity andmission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests on agreed formats, and other documentary requirements.
