title: Research Manager
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON REACH**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to lead our research team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 1 year, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027.

## **Country profile**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea.

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community in Somalia. Data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to directly inform humanitarian response planning, as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Key areas of focus include:

**Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA):** REACH conducts the annual MSNA, whose findings feed into the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) workshop and, through it, the annual Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

**Food Security and Nutrition:** REACH conducts food security and nutrition assessments that feed into Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition analyses.

**Cash and Markets:** REACH provides research and analytical support to the Somali Cash Consortium and conducts market monitoring analysis as part of a harmonised approach, led by the Cash Working Group.

**Ad-hoc Research:** REACH conducts ad-hoc assessments as needs arise, including rapid needs assessments following sudden-onset shocks such as flooding, drought and conflict-induced displacement.

To ensure that research findings meaningfully inform humanitarian response planning, REACH shares data through formal coordination platforms, including the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), needs analysis and planning processes, the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, among others. Partner feedback is actively integrated to validate and triangulate findings, as well as to guide research design and geographic targeting.

## **FUNCTIONS**

REACH is seeking an experienced candidate who has previously managed teams and implemented projects in a complex humanitarian setting. Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, and in close coordination with the Country Representative and HQ, the Research Manager will be responsible for overseeing the implementation, development, and strategy of the research portfolio of the REACH Somalia mission. This includes managing the teams responsible for the MSNA, food security and nutrition assessments, the Somali Cash Consortium, market monitoring, and ad-hoc assessments such as rapid needs assessments.

The candidate should be comfortable representing REACH with donors and be able to coordinate and liaise with a range of senior external partners, including OCHA, cluster coordinators, UN agencies and NGOs. This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, humanitarian cluster, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager’s responsibilities include the following:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Direct management of international and national research staff across the MSNA, food security and nutrition, cash and markets, and ad-hoc assessment workstreams, including recruitment, appraisals, and capacity building;
- Day-to-day management of the research team, including the development of work plans and performance indicators, and development and implementation of capacity training plans to improve efficiency and performance;
- Conduct regular check-ins with staff within the unit, and promote team building, productivity and staff welfare as the main pastoral focal point for research staff;
- Provide regular support and technical backstopping;
- Take on additional work streams and management responsibilities as well as advise in strategic mission decision-making as a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), as required.

***RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant project and programme objectives, and REACH’s research cycle guidelines;
- Ensure that all (Senior) Research Officers are comprehensively briefed on objectives and expected outputs of research cycles, and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood;
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation for an assessment;
- For each research cycle, review ToRs before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that ToRs are validated before data collection begins;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning, data collection, and management;
- Monitor data collection, ensuring correct implementation in line with agreed ToRs, and keep track of progress and delays of all assessments throughout the research cycle;
- Work closely with the Field Manager and Ops teams to ensure logistics, finance, administration, security and HR processes directly related to REACH are appropriately implemented, alongside the relevant Acted departments.

***PORTFOLIO OVERSIGHT***

- Oversee the timely delivery of the annual MSNA, ensuring that findings are available in time to feed into the JIAF workshop and the HNRP, and support the team in preparing for and participating in the JIAF process;
- Oversee food security and nutrition assessments, ensuring that methodologies, timelines and outputs are aligned with IPC requirements and that data is made available to IPC analyses as planned;
- Oversee REACH’s research support to the Somali Cash Consortium, ensuring that deliverables meet consortium and donor requirements and timelines;
- Oversee market monitoring analysis, ensuring consistent, timely outputs that are used by Cash Working Group partners;
- Lead the planning and rapid deployment of ad-hoc assessments, such as rapid needs assessments, in response to emerging crises and partner information needs, in coordination with OCHA and the clusters.

***ANALYSIS AND DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure research staff maintain regular communication with HQ on progress and deadlines for written products;
- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs (i.e. reports, factsheets, briefs, presentations, etc.), complying with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Review all research products before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- Under supervision of HQ, ensure that research products are uploaded to relevant data portals, as specified in research ToRs;
- Under the direction of the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, engage in the dissemination of research products, including emails, presentations to coordination bodies, and bilateral meetings, such as with donors;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in conducting monitoring and evaluation as specified in the research ToRs and in line with REACH guidelines.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- With the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, identify information gaps in line with humanitarian priorities in Somalia, and identify advocacy and dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of REACH’s work;
- Lead on formalising synergies with other assessment and knowledge management actors, as well as strategic partnerships with key humanitarian stakeholders and decision makers;
- As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Somalia country strategy.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Represent REACH at the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG) and in other inter-agency coordination forums, and act as a key REACH focal point for OCHA on needs analysis and humanitarian programme cycle processes;
- Represent REACH in cluster and multi-sector meetings and technical working groups, including the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, and follow up on technical issues identified in these forums;
- In coordination with the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, present research findings to relevant partners to enhance their use and impact;
- Ensure that external communications with partners and key stakeholders, including UN agencies, local and national authorities, and NGOs, are conducted and documented as appropriate;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in external engagement on REACH strategy and, when requested, in fundraising and grants management.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs, and will ensure that the research team does the same. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

The Research Manager is also responsible for ensuring that all interactions with crisis-affected populations are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner, and that communities are adequately consulted and informed about REACH programme objectives, activities and methodologies.

## **REQUIREMEnTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international relations, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, social research, or similar).
- **Years of work experience** At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis.
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative research experience, including sampling, methodology design and analysis. Ability to provide technical oversight of research products to a high standard.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Experience with the humanitarian programme cycle (HNRP/JIAF) and with humanitarian coordination forums (e.g. ICCG, clusters) is strongly preferred.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA-type research, food security and nutrition assessments and/or IPC processes, and cash and markets research is highly desirable.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high-level presentations and briefings to senior external audiences.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to manage multiple research cycles in parallel with tight deadlines in a complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the Horn of Africa region is desirable, or in any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’660 **CHF** and 3’720 **CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 **USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees

title: Senior Research Officer
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our team in Somalia.**

**Department**:REACH

**Position**:Senior Research Officer

**Contract duration**:4 months, with high likelihood of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu

**Starting Date**: 7 September 2026

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Research Manager, the Senior Research Officer is responsible for the implementation of IMPACT’s MSNA research cycle in Somalia, including the preparation, data collection, analysis, drafting, dissemination, and evaluation stages. Throughout the MSNA, the Senior Research Officer engages with partners and stakeholders to promote their participation and maximize their impact. They also ensure an efficient and transparent use of resources required for project implementation.

This position requires strong research skills (particularly in quantitative and mixed methodology sampling), willingness to work in hardship location, an analytical mind, creativity, independence, and an interest in the national and regional context. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings, as well as engage with external stakeholders in the design and dissemination of the research cycle. The position will regularly require interpreting data, highlighting relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research.

BACKGROUND OF MULTI SECTORAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT

IMPACT HQ in Geneva support the work of Multi-Sector Needs Assessments (MSNAs) in more than 20 countries. As a result of the World Humanitarian Summit and the Grand Bargain, a commitment was made to “impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context sensitive, timely and up to date” joint needs assessments that can serve as “a sound evidence base for humanitarian response plans”. These exercises have been informing consolidated humanitarian appeals since 2016. Since 2016, the number of MSNAs supported by REACH has more than quadrupled; MSNA data continues to influence flagship humanitarian response processes such as Humanitarian Needs and Response Plans (HNRPs). This indicates that evidence-based decision making is increasingly becoming a cornerstone of effective humanitarian action.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Research Officer is responsibilities include:

***Research CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Anticipate knowledge gaps prior to the execution of a Research Cycle through strong understanding of the Somali context.
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation of an assessment.
- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant research and project objectives and with IMPACT’s research cycle and other relevant guidelines.
- Design research approaches and methodologies according to IMPACT’s requirements and principles as well as partners’ information needs.
- Compose and construct, in close coordination with GIS and data teams, qualitative and quantitative data collection tool.
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in research design and planning.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING***

- Line manage the MSNA Research Officer directly and lead the MSNA team throughout the research cycle
- In close liaison with the Field Manager and Ops teams (field officer and logistics team), manage assessment logistics, including with partner organizations, identifying assessment areas, facilitating design workshops, managing joint data collection processes, and facilitating joint analysis workshops.
- In close liaison the Ops teams, ensure logistics, financial, administration, security and HR processes directly related to ongoing and upcoming assessments are appropriately planned, implemented and coordinated with the relevant Acted departments.
- In close liaison with data colleagues, provide quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data analysis on primary and/or secondary data as per ToRs, ensuring that meaningful techniques are used to analyze the data collected.
- Promoting capacity building across the IMPACT Somalia mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience)
- Providing day-to-day direct and indirect management of the research team within their unit/workstream, and field team during data collection.
    
    ***Internal Coordination***
- Interacting autonomously with HQ departments and serve as mission focal point for HQ’s corresponding unit and specialists in particular themes or technical areas.
- Engage in the development and implementation of IMPACT’s strategy in Somalia
- Conduct regular meetings with relevant national and international assessment staff members to assess progress in relevant research cycles and to review work plan.
- For all activities, ensure that all assessment and field teams are comprehensively briefed on objectives, expected outputs and that the overall implementation strategy is clearly understood.
- Ensure that project/field staff are given required training and resources to achieve their tasks in line with IMPACT and project requirements. Support to the line managers and specialists in the development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Be available to provide regular support and technical backstopping; regularly debrief team members to receive feedback on the progress of an activity.
- In coordination with line manager, contribute to conduct induction for new staff members, including training in basic technical competencies for research design, implementation and analysis.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs that consolidate the analyses from each research cycle into relevant products such as factsheets, reports, briefs, presentations, etc which comply with IMPACT’s guidelines and quality standards.
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact in line with their intended use for the relevant audiences.
- Follow the designated timeline of reports to be submitted to project partners and donors. Ensure that delays or identified challenges for specific assessments are reported in writing and orally in a timely manner.
- Maintain regular communication with country Management and IMPACT HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ before external release.

***External Engagement***

- Ensure that relevant partners are consulted and involved at all stages of research cycle: assessment preparation; data collection; data analysis; review of research products; product dissemination; and lessons learnt.
- After validation by the line manager, represent IMPACT in relevant external meetings/ working groups.
- Follow up on issues identified by partners or during meetings / working groups.
- Promote an active use of datasets and research findings by partners and the broader humanitarian community for their decision making.
- After validation by line manager, disseminate research findings to relevant third parties in order to enhance their use and impact.
- Ensure that all partner engagement and all external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues.
- More generally, contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of IMPACT’s mandate, ethics, values and stand-point with regard to other actors.

***Data Confidentiality and Protection***

- The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOPs. He/she will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis, etc.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience required. Ability to adapt, implement and interpret methodology, sampling and analysis to a high standard
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA type of research and humanitarian assessments is an asset. Prior experience working with components of FSL/public health is highly desirable
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills for effective and accurate reporting required
- **Academic** **qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Master’s degree in relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, etc)
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Advanced skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage; Experience with InDesign an asset.
- **Level of independence** Proven ability to work independently.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the HoA region is desirable; or any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between **3’000 CHF** and **3’120 CHF** monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of **300 USD**
- NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. IMPACT is hosted by Acted in this country \[to be adjusted depending on the country\]
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Diaspora as Anticipatory Actors in Conflict-Induced Displacement Consultancy
body:
Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

## Purpose of the consultancy

Under the project Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD), the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and DEMAC are commissioning a consultancy to consolidate lessons and findings on the role of diaspora in anticipatory action under the project. The consultancy focuses on two levels:

**(1) Context monitoring, community sensing and early warning:** examining whether diaspora and local partner specific signals, including remittance patterns and community sensing indicators, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement; and,

**(2) Response and activation:** the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, including how they mobilise resources quickly and exploring other innovative modalities for channelling support.

## Background

AHEAD — Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement — is a global project led by the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) that aims to strengthen humanitarian responses by improving the ability to act before displacement occurs. Implemented in eight countries (Yemen, Myanmar, Somalia, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Uganda, South Sudan), it combines in-country implementation with cross-context learning to build an evidence base for anticipatory action (AA) in conflict settings — an area far less developed than AA for climatic shocks. A key component of the project is to strengthen the inclusion of diaspora and local actors in designing AA frameworks and supporting their engagement in preparedness, early warning dissemination, and rolling out AA responses.

Diaspora, often outside formal humanitarian structures, play an essential role in conflict-prone contexts. Sitting at the intersection of a layered, real-time information ecosystem, they occupy a unique position of trust and access that formal systems cannot replicate, receiving real-time community intelligence — often within hours — and disseminating warnings through channels, communities actually listen to in areas hard to reach. The same trusted channels that receive community intelligence also serve as the fastest available mechanism for mobilising and transferring resources. Across crises, they share unique capacities to mobilise and transfer resources swiftly, rapidly and innovatively, serving as often overlooked yet critical lifelines that are sustained beyond the lifespan of a crisis. This dual function of sensing and acting is what makes diaspora actors uniquely positioned in the AA ecosystem, and what distinguishes them from other formal early warning actors.

Yet while diaspora actors are increasingly recognised as informal humanitarian actors and vital responders in the aftermath of crisis, their capacity to mobilise existing knowledge, networks and resources in the critical window *before* displacement peaks remains largely under-conceptualised and under-examined. This gap extends across both dimensions of diaspora engagement: the signals they detect and the modalities through which they mobilise support. Remittances are illustrative. As a signal, shifts in remittance behaviour may point to deteriorating conditions in real time — when communities begin planning their displacement journey — yet their reliability and specificity as an early warning indicator remain untested. And while Somali remittances exceed USD 2 billion annually, outpacing official development assistance and humanitarian aid combined, these flows are inherently kinship-based and solidarity-driven, mediated by relations of trust and reciprocity, and mobilised almost exclusively in reaction to crises that have already hit. Accordingly, this raises broader questions about whether their support can be relied upon proactively, and/or sustained across recurrent shocks without exhausting the networks they depend on. Across both the predictive and the financing dimensions, it remains unexamined whether diaspora signals and resources — remittances among them — can be oriented towards anticipatory ends. This is the conceptual and empirical gap the consultancy sets out to explore and address.

This consultancy is anchored in the AHEAD Somalia context - a context that combines recurrent, overlapping conflict- and climate-driven displacement with an exceptionally strong, densely connected diaspora. As AHEAD is implemented in Somalia, DRC and its partners generate evidence on two questions: whether the signals diaspora detect are reliable enough to act on, and how their engagement affects outcomes once a response is triggered. The consultancy's role is to consolidate this evidence and package it into a structured account of diaspora as anticipatory actors. In doing so, the consultancy seeks to position diaspora as a missing piece in AA systems, with the Somalia experience presenting an emerging, largely unexplored frontier whose lessons could strengthen how anticipatory action is designed, funded and activated across other contexts.

Because this work concerns anticipation, its object is inherently uncertain — whether a predicted crisis will take place, and when or how often partners activate, cannot be known in advance; the consultancy is therefore designed to follow the implementation as it unfolds and adapt to what it surfaces, rather than evaluate predetermined events.

## Objective of the consultancy

The consultant will consolidate and package the evidence generated under the project by DRC across four learning areas. The guiding questions under each set out what the consolidated learning should answer.

Across these areas, the consultant will be required to:

1. **Context monitoring, community sensing and early warning:** Examine and consolidate findings on whether signals reported by diaspora and local partners, namely shifts in remittance patterns and community sensing data gathered under the AHEAD project, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

Sub-questions:

1. *Can changes in remittance patterns — spikes or drops in transfer volumes, frequency, and requests — serve as a reliable early warning indicator for conflict-induced displacement, and/or as an earlier precursor of crisis?*
    1. *Can social signals related to community sensing, including social media monitoring and social pattern detection serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement, and/or as earlier precursors of crisis?*
2. **Activation – Response:** Examine and consolidate lessons on the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, and how their engagement affects outcomes (assessed against indicators such as access, speed and trust). This includes capturing lessons from innovative modalities for support emerging from AHEAD’s implementation in Somalia. Among these, DRC is currently exploring trigger-based payments that connect early warning triggers to diaspora transfers ahead of a predicted crisis; should this be taken forward, it would form part of this learning.

Sub-questions:

1. *How does diaspora engagement in AA implementation affect outcomes for affected communities — e.g. reach to hard-to-reach groups, trust, acceptance, complementarity with the formal response, and associated risks?*
2. *How do the speed and modality of diaspora financial support affect AA outcomes?*
3. *What innovative modalities for channelling diaspora support emerge through AHEAD's implementation in Somalia, such as trigger-based payments, and what conditions, infrastructure and partnerships are needed for them to work as anticipatory funding ahead of a predicted crisis?*
4. **Linking Informal to Formal EW/AA Structures:** Examine and consolidate lessons on the conditions, benefits and risks of connecting diaspora and community-based early warning (EW) structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism across both the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle.

Sub-questions:

1. *What conditions proved necessary for diaspora and community-based EW structures to connect effectively to the AHEAD AA response mechanism across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle?*
    1. *What benefits and risks did this surface for the actors involved — including effects on community ownership, diaspora–local partner trust, and responsiveness to warnings?*
2. **Cross-Cutting - Learning & Advocacy**: Package the consolidated learning into case studies for external publication and a synthesis report to inform AHEAD and broader diaspora programming, drawing out implications for scaling to other contexts.

## Scope of work and Methodology

The consultant will prepare a **methodology and work plan** setting out how the evidence generated in-house will be consolidated and packaged against the objectives above, and the support required from DRC and DEMAC.

**Division of roles:** All primary data collection, triangulation and assessment is carried out in-house. DRC's AHEAD team and partners collect early warning and monitoring data, including bi-weekly reporting from diaspora–local partner pairs; DRC's MEAL and data teams triangulate and assess this data, together with activation and outcome data. The consultant complements this with targeted qualitative fieldwork on remittance flows and community sensing (objective 1) and on the diaspora contribution in activation (objective 2), and consolidates the evidence and findings generated in-house and package them into the outputs set out below. Accordingly, the consultancy will work in a very coordinated manner with the data and MEAL team to avoid potential duplications.

**Indicative scope:** the evidence covers diaspora–local partner pairs across four or five locations in Gedo (Luuq and Beled Xawo) and Hiraan (BeledWeyne, Jalalaqsi, and Buulo Burte (TBC)), including bi-weekly monitoring data from all (up to five) and activation in up to three locations (AHEAD target locations; eg. Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi). The number and timing of activations cannot be known in advance.

The learning notes produced under **areas 1–3 serve as interim outputs**, feeding into the final synthesis report and policy brief.

All deliverables are to be submitted in English. Fieldwork will be conducted in Somali

The main tasks related to achieving the above-mentioned objectives are described in detail below:

**Scope**

**Deliverables**

**Suggested Activities**

**Community context monitoring (objective 1)** Examine and consolidate findings on whether signals reported by diaspora and local partners, namely shifts in remittance patterns and community sensing data gathered under the AHEAD project, can serve as reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

1 learning note on whether diaspora and community sensing signals are reliable early warning indicators for conflict-induced displacement.

Consolidate DRC in-house context monitoring data (which will cross-compare and triangulate indicators received from diaspora and local partners with DRC community context monitoring) an carry out complementary qualitative fieldwork examining how remittance flows (including mobile money transfers) and community sensing signals shift ahead of displacement.

n each of the four to five target locations, this includes around 5 (five) key informant interviews (with mobile money agents or remittance providers, local partners, community leaders and local authorities) and 1 (one) focus group discussion with recipient households. In addition, around 8 (eight) remote interviews with diaspora senders.

Findings feed into the assessment of reliability, timeliness, accuracy, bias and conflict sensitivity.

**Activation – Response (objective 2)** Examine and consolidate lessons on the distinctive contribution diaspora organisations and their local partners make in the partial and full activation phases, and how their engagement affects outcomes (assessed against indicators such as access, speed and trust). This includes capturing lessons from innovative modalities for support emerging from AHEAD’s implementation in Somalia.

1 learning report on the diaspora contribution in activation, including resource mobilisation and innovative modalities (which could include trigger-based payments)

Complement in-house activation and outcome data with qualitative fieldwork to assess the quality, relevance and acceptance of diaspora and local partner assistance across partial and full activation, including the speed and modalities of resource mobilisation. In each location where activation takes place (up to three), this includes around five key informant interviews (with local partners, community leaders, local authorities and other responders) and two to three focus group discussions with affected communities.

Capture lessons from innovative modalities for support, including trigger-based payments if taken forward.

Quantitative impact data on needs mitigation following AA assistance will be provided by in-house MEAL Specialist. Measurable outcome analysis is provided in-house by MEAL Specialist.

**Linking Informal to Formal EW/AA Structures (objective 3):** Through after-action review, assess the conditions, benefits and risks of connecting diaspora and community-based early warning (EW) structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism, across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle.

1 assessment of connecting informal diaspora and community EW structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism.

Consolidate lessons and support AHEAD team in conducting after-action review, examining the connection at each stage of the cycle — monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation — drawing on the evidence from areas 1 and 2.

**Cross-Cutting – Learning & Advocacy (objective 4):** Generate case studies for external publication and a synthesis report to inform AHEAD and broader diaspora programming, and assess implications for scaling to other contexts.

3 Case studies for external publication; a final synthesis report and policy brief.

Document case studies from AHEAD's implementation in Somalia; produce interim learning notes; present findings at AHEAD convenings; deliver the final synthesis report and policy brief with recommendations on diaspora inclusion in AA and implications for scaling.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will submit the following deliverables as mentioned below:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description of tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Phase 1 — Inception & baseline**

1 Inception report with approved methodology and work plan

Kick-off meeting; agree methodology and work plan with DRC

5 working days (4 lead / 1 field team) over period Q4 2026

**Phase 2 — Context monitoring**

1 Learning note on the reliability of diaspora and community-sensing signals as early warning

Consolidate in-house monitoring data and analysis; carry out fieldwork across the four to five target locations (ie. Luuq and Beled Xawo (Gedo), and BeledWeyne, Jalalaqsi and Buulo Burte TBC) (Hiraan) (key informant interviews and focus group discussions) and remote interviews with diaspora senders.

35 working days (15 lead / 20 field team). over period Q1-Q2 2027

**Phase 3 — Activation & response**

1 Learning report on the diaspora contribution in activation, including resource mobilisation and the feasibility of trigger-based payments

Consolidate in-house activation and outcome data; Qualitatively examine diaspora engagement across partial and full activation (up to three locations); capture lessons from innovative modalities for support, including trigger-based payments if taken forward.

40 working days (18 lead / 22 field team) over period Q1–Q3 2027, following activation as it occurs

**Phase 4 — Linking informal to formal**

1 After-action review assessment of connecting diaspora and community EW structures to the AHEAD AA response mechanism

After-action review across the monitoring, reporting, escalation and activation cycle, drawing on the evidence from Phases 2 and 3

10 working days (8 lead / 2 field team) over period of Q2–Q3 2027

**Phase 5 — Cross-cutting & synthesis**

3 case studies for external publication; 1 final synthesis report and 1 policy brief

Produce case studies to present findings at AHEAD convenings; deliver the final synthesis report and 1 policy brief with recommendations and implications for scaling across contexts.

20 total working days (18 field team / 2 local).(Case studies run alongside Phases 2–4 (Q1–Q3 2027); final report and policy brief by 1st September 2027.

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The assignment involves up **to 110 working days** spread over a contract period of up to 10 months, from December 2026 to 30 September 2027. **Payment is linked to approved deliverables, not to days worked.**

- **Instalment 1:** Inception report, data collection tools and fieldwork plan (Phase 1) – 30%
- **Instalment 2:** Learning note on context monitoring and early warning & Activations (Phase 2 & 3) – 20%
- **Instalment 3:** Learning note on linking informal to formal structures & Case studies, final synthesis report and policy brief (Phase 4 & 5) – 50%

The consultant shall be prepared to complete the assignment no later than **30 September 2027.**

The level of effort is **expected to vary throughout the assignment**. Periods of higher intensity are anticipated during the inception phase, including the development of the methodology and workplan, and during the final synthesis and evaluation phase, including analysis, reporting, and dissemination of findings. Additional periods of increased effort may arise in connection with activation events and response monitoring; however, the timing and frequency of such activations cannot be determined in advance and will depend on contextual developments.

Should fewer activations occur than anticipated, days allocated to Phase 3 may be reallocated to other deliverables, as agreed with DRC.

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

**Eligibility**

- The bidder is a research or consultancy firm registered as a legal entity in its country of incorporation; individual consultants are not eligible.
- The firm proposes a named team leader and a field research team meeting the profiles below.

**Experience**

**Firm:**

- At least 2 years since registration
- Proven track record delivering qualitative research or evaluations, ideally in humanitarian or conflict settings
- At least three research, evaluation or review assignments for international organisations, research institutes or development agencies, preferably in the Horn of Africa[\[SO6\]](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_6)
- Record of producing publishable outputs (reports, policy briefs, case studies)
- Ability to access and work safely in the target locations in Gedo and Hiraan

Desirable: established presence or research network in Somalia; familiarity with anticipatory action and community-based early warning

**Proposed Composition of Team**

**Team leader**

- Master's degree or PhD in social sciences, development studies, peace and conflict studies or a related field; a PhD is an asset
- At least 5 years' post-graduate research experience in humanitarian, displacement or conflict settings in the Horn of Africa
- Demonstrated research on the Somali diaspora, diaspora humanitarianism or remittances, evidenced by at least two publications or research projects
- Strong research design, qualitative analysis and after-action review skills
- Demonstrated ability to synthesise and package findings into high-quality, publishable outputs (reports, briefs, case studies)
- Experience overseeing qualitative fieldwork (FGDs, KIIs) in Somalia, including in hard-to-reach areas, and coordinating in-country researchers
- Established access to, and trust with, relevant diaspora and local actors (desirable)
- Excellent written and spoken English required, fluency in Somali is an asset.

**Field research team:**

- At least 3 years of field-research experience in Somalia; research experience in Gedo or Hiraan is an asset
- Somali-speaking field researchers able to conduct key informant interviews and focus group discussions in target locations
- Deep knowledge of Somalia and its context — clan and community structures, conflict and displacement dynamics
- Established access to, and trust with relevant local actors and communities in the target areas

## Technical supervision

### The selected consultant will work under the supervision of: ***DRC Diaspora AA lead***

*In close coordination with the DRC AHEAD team, including DRC AA Lead/PM at country office and regional level (EAGL) and DRC data team.*

## Location and support

Remote or based in East Africa.

The Firm will provide her/his own computer and mobile telephone.

## Travel

The assignment is expected to be mainly remote for the team leader. The financial bid should include all travel and fieldwork costs( travel, accommodation, meals etc), based on a minimum of:

- One field round in each of the four confirmed target locations during Phase 2 (Luuq, Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi), plus Buulo Burte if confirmed
- One field round in each location where activation takes place during Phase 3 (up to three, expected to be Beled Xawo, BeledWeyne and Jalalaqsi)

title: Education Project Manager Ethiopia North Afar
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is seeking a dynamic, experienced and results-oriented **Roving Education Project Manager** to lead the development and delivery of quality education programmes across its Northern operations.

Based in Asayita, you will drive the design, planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of education interventions, spanning rapid emergency education responses, formal and non-formal education, transitional education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). You will play a key role in identifying education needs, developing project proposals, mobilising resources and ensuring that programmes remain responsive to the evolving needs of crisis-affected communities.

Working closely with Area Office management, the Country Office Education team, local authorities, consortium partners and other stakeholders, you will provide technical and operational leadership to ensure programme quality, effective resource management, accountability and compliance with donor requirements and humanitarian standards. You will also strengthen team capacity, promote safe and inclusive learning environments, and champion child-friendly feedback mechanisms that expand access to relevant, quality education.

We are looking for a leader who can turn education needs into practical, sustainable interventions and help children and young people affected by displacement and crisis - including refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and vulnerable host-community members - access safe, inclusive and meaningful learning opportunities.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals.*

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDIj7IeschNSqrBZXGOJidmAb50QM0xCWzaSK9uhnNS4iw?e=4aaUB1) for more generic & specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Coordinate with Area Office management to ensure the effective planning, implementation, and quality delivery of children and youth programming and foundational education activities.
- Proper oversight, management and build capacity of education teams to operationalize quality, timely and comprehensive education programming
- Ensure the effective use of existing monitoring and evaluation systems in collaboration with the Education team, and work with the Country Office to develop, adapt, and streamline Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) tools to strengthen programme quality, responsiveness, accountability, and learning.
- Promote inclusion, gender and accountability within all education programme
- Support and contribute to implementation of NRC Education Workstreams and strategies
- Ensure quality control of education activities through the development and rollout of output and outcome level monitoring and evaluation tools, guidelines and procedures and its timely and proper reporting.
- Prepare, participation and contribute to Grant Opening, Regular Project review session and BVA meeting to provide updates on work, spending and procurement plans,
- Onsite field monitoring and analyses contextual trends and changes and assess the education needs of children and youth to identify gaps in service provision and inform appropriate, timely, and needs-based programming for crisis-affected populations.
- Contribute to the development of the NRC education strategy and macro-log frame, theories of change, and NRC education work-plan and ensure they link to other Core Competencies
- Demonstrated experience in the successful design, planning, coordination, and implementation of first-line emergency education responses, formal and non-formal education programmes, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes in Ethiopia,
- Ensuring programme quality, timely delivery, relevance to local needs, and alignment with NRC’s education strategy and humanitarian standards.
- Oversee the implementation of Safe and Inclusive Programming (SIP) standards across all NRC education activities, ensuring compliance with NRC policies and guidelines and that all reported safeguarding concerns or breaches are appropriately referred, addressed, and resolved in accordance with established procedures.
- Ensure the effective integration and continuous use of child-friendly feedback and complaint mechanisms across the Education portfolio.
- Ensure compliance with NRC financial, administrative, logistical, and procurement procedures within the Education team.
- Oversee the overall budget management of Education projects implemented in the Area Office, monitor expenditure, spending levels rates, and assures no under- or overspending.
- Lead the development of project plans, proposals, budgets, and project extensions in collaboration with relevant programme and support teams, ensuring alignment with NRC strategies, donor requirements, and identified needs.

**What you will bring:**

- Education- Master’s degree in education planning and management (EDPM), Curriculum Studies, Educational Psychology, Education in Emergencies, or a related field.
- Professional Experience- At least five years of relevant experience in the education sector, preferably in humanitarian, emergency response, or recovery contexts, including a minimum of three years in project management or an equivalent leadership role.
- Technical Expertise- Extensive experience in implementing first-line emergency education responses, formal and non-formal education programmes, and Technical and Vocational Training (TVET) programmes in Ethiopia.
- Experience of working in complex and volatile contexts
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- Knowledge and leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal
- Knowledge of the context in Ethiopia
- Contextual understanding and knowledge of the Education sector and stakeholders in Ethiopia
- Familiarity with Education related minimum standards
- Strong communication skills ensuring good relations and smooth operations with stakeholders.
- Detail-oriented and strong analytical skills
- Strong project management skills

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Asayita, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Regional Solutions Adviser - Syria & Hosting Countries
body:
**What we are looking for**

Candidates with management/advisory level experience within the humanitarian context, specifically those with deep understanding of the Syria context, displacement dynamics, and durable solutions frameworks.

To succeed in this role candidates will need to be strong and experienced in donor engagement, business development, and grant management, as well as experience in project management i.e. coordinating and managing programmes across multiple countries and stakeholders.

Strong strategic planning, analytical, and communication skills are also a requirement for this position.

**What you will do**

The **Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)** is seeking a strategic and experienced humanitarian professional to join our MENA Regional Office as Regional Solutions Adviser - Syria & Hosting Countries.

As the region continues to navigate displacement, return preparedness, and durable solutions for Syrians, this pivotal role will drive regional collaboration, strengthen programme quality, and support innovative, multi-country responses across **Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, and the wider MENA region**.

You will play a leading role in shaping NRC's regional Syria response by:

- Providing strategic programme support and guidance to country offices.
- Strengthening cross-country coordination, learning, and regional coherence.
- Leading the development and management of regional and multi-country grants.
- Identifying and securing new funding opportunities and donor partnerships.
- Supporting return preparedness and durable solutions initiatives for Syrian refugees and returnees.
- Coordinating scenario planning, information sharing, and regional analysis.
- Representing NRC in relevant regional forums and stakeholder engagements.
- Promoting evidence-based programming, learning, and advocacy across the Syria response.

**What you will bring**

We are seeking a collaborative and forward-thinking adviser with:

- 6-8 years of humanitarian, recovery, or development experience, including 3 years in advisory or management roles.
- Specialist knowledge and expertise equivalent to an advanced university degree in a relevant field (e.g., international development, politics, social science)
- Strong knowledge of development and other institutional donors’ strategies, priorities, and compliance requirements for relevant donors.
- Track record of successful proposal development, or similar in funding or partnerships
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts, with preference for previous experience in the region
- Understanding of, and commitment to working collaboratively with technical and operational colleagues within a matrix structure, including capacity building
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal

**Context related skills, knowledge and experience**

- Deep knowledge and understanding of the Syria context
- Experience with coordination role across different countries
- Experience working with overall strategy development and planning
- Experience of developing learning and development tools and resources to support capacity building
- Understanding of durable solutions concepts and frameworks and previous experience in working on return contexts
- Experience with project management, including budget monitoring, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting, modification requests and evaluations
- Knowledge of and interest in new business opportunities, including different partnerships modalities, grants and commercial opportunities
- Experience of working with cross-country programmes and donors

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAM0Gl5p5UvRIDRI7Z6ESKdAc0K_8qqUHKieitun5UJxOg?e=HdWSf7) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman Jordan, Syria or Lebanon. **Please note that this is a non-accompanied position.**
- Fixed term contract: Until November 2027 (extension possible if additional funding is secured)
- Travel: Up to 30% to Field locations.
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from all qualified candidates.
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

**If you're passionate about regional leadership, partnership-building, and developing solutions for displaced populations, we'd love to hear from you.**

**Apply today and help shape the future of NRC's Syria & Hosting countries' response.**

title: Monitoring Officer - Roster
body:
**Monitoring Officer - Roster**

**Summary**

**Languages:** One of 12 roster languages (Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini and Somali), plus English and/or Arabic and/or French.

**Role:** Structured monitoring phone calls with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors.

**Based:** Remote, from anywhere.

**Roster:** Unpaid standby pool from January 2027 to May 2029. Joining is not a job offer.

**Reports to:** M&E Lead.

**Contract:** Consultancy contract per campaign.

## **Why this roster**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) is a three-year project funded by the EU’s Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF). It is built around Seefar’s Crisis Adaptation Mechanism (CAM), which lets the project respond when migration patterns shift. When a monitored indicator crosses its threshold, a campaign may be activated for a new audience or language, and Seefar then has two weeks to launch it. That is too short to recruit from scratch, so we keep an unpaid standby pool of vetted Counsellors, Social Media Officers and Monitoring Officers for 12 languages, ready to be contracted the moment a campaign is approved.

## **Who we are**

Seefar Foundation is a social enterprise with a simple mission: to transform the lives of vulnerable people. Through programmes rooted in technology, psychology and behaviour change, we help people build the skills and confidence they need to make a positive contribution to their communities. It’s how we support governments in finding solutions to challenges around irregular migration, poverty, human trafficking, violent extremism, access to justice, and more.

Our exceptional team of over 100 consultants are problem solvers and innovators, delivering programmes and high impact research. Together, we solve difficult, high impact problems for governments and NGOs across communications, digital, and research, monitoring and evaluation in Africa, Asia, and Europe.

## **Your Responsibilities**

1. Checkback calls (80%). Take part in a paid introductory training session and get to know the campaign, the checkback tools and the ethical guidelines for engaging with vulnerable people. Then conduct structured checkback calls by phone with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors at 3 weeks, 3 months or 12 months after their one-to-one support session with a Seefar counsellor. Administer the standardised checkback tools (Kobo forms) consistently on every call, capturing quantitative and qualitative data on wellbeing, migration decisions, referrals and satisfaction with the support received. Submit completed records within 24 hours of each call.
2. Data quality and learning (15%). Share observations on patterns in responses, data quality issues and anything that may affect the reliability of findings. Support translation or back-translation of M&E tools and templates between your language and English when needed. Manage your own call schedule and flag promptly when participants cannot be reached.
3. Independence and safeguarding (5%). Because checkbacks are a quality control process, stay independent of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, so that outcome data remains neutral and credible. Treat all participant data with strict confidentiality in line with Seefar’s data protection standards, and escalate safeguarding concerns immediately.

## **Who you are**

**To succeed, you’ll need:**

- At least 3 years’ experience in monitoring and evaluation, data collection or a related field.
- Experience conducting structured telephone or remote surveys or interviews.
- Fluency in at least one roster language, and working proficiency in written and spoken English and/or Arabic and/or French.
- Computer literacy and a reliable internet connection.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, and the ability to engage sensitively with vulnerable people.
- The ability to work independently and remotely, and manage your own workload against deadlines.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- A private, quiet space for confidential calls.
- The ability to work as an independent consultant and receive payments in EUR by international bank transfer.

You should meet all of the above. It’s a bonus if you have experience on humanitarian, development or migration-related programmes, familiarity with psychosocial support or returnee contexts, or experience using Kobo Toolbox or similar platforms.

## **How you work**

**Spoken/Written English and/or French and/or Arabic**

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You interview fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Structured interviewing**

You follow a questionnaire consistently, without sounding scripted.

**Sensitivity**

You put people at ease, recognise distress and respond with care.

**Data accuracy**

The data you collect is complete, consistent and entered within 24 hours.

**Independence**

You keep a clear boundary from the delivery team so data stays credible.

**Translation**

You translate and back-translate M&E tools accurately.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with Kobo or similar tools and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact Monitoring Officers about six weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to NPR’s M&E Lead. To keep outcome data neutral, you will work independently of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, while sharing what you learn with the M&E team. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

Women counsellors are especially needed for the Somali-speaking pool.

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You counsel fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Empathy**

You stay calm, patient and present with people in distress.

**Assessment**

You recognise distress and mental health needs, and respond appropriately.

**Information**

You explain migration risks and safe, legal alternatives without judgement.

**Confidentiality**

You protect participants’ data and know when to raise safeguarding concerns.

**Record keeping**

You document every session on time, every time.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with using a laptop or phone and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact counsellors about three weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to the Project Coordinator, or to a team leader on larger campaigns, and work alongside other counsellors. The Social Media Officer’s campaign brings people to you, and Monitoring Officers later check back, independently, with a sample of the people you counselled. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

 This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.
