 The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

 This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

 **Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

**Job Requirements:**

**Knowledge & Experience**

- 6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
- Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
- Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
- Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
- Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

**Personal Attributes**

- Spanish language proficiency
- Builds credibility quickly with leadership
- Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
- Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

**Working Environment*****:***

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $132,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Program Officer, Catalyst
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

Across the U.S. and Europe, IRC's Resettlement, Asylum, and Integration (RAI) department works to strengthen the systems that surround newcomers, building the capacity of service providers, governments, and communities to plan, coordinate, and deliver services more effectively. Over the past decade, this work has reached tens of thousands of learners through more than 50 projects across 13 countries and all 50 U.S. states.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer to support the implementation of Catalyst, RAI’s new systems strengthening identity. Catalyst draws on IRC's expertise in learning, research, programmatic excellence, partnerships, and AI-enabled delivery to help governments and organizations build stronger, more coordinated systems that deliver accessible, high-quality services to newcomers. Through systems strengthening work, Catalyst advances RAI's Impact@Scale priorities of Legal Services, Workforce Development, and Connected Communities.

This role will focus on project management and coordination of various Catalyst systems strengthening projects. The position will lead cross-team coordination among multiple contributors, support strategy and outreach efforts, manage deliverables using Switchboard’s project management tools, and ensure timely, high-quality completion of work across multiple initiatives. This role reports to the Senior Program Officer for Catalyst and will work closely with teams across Switchboard and the IRC.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Serve as the designated project manager for state-specific training and capacity-building initiatives.
- Manage projects across multiple teams, establishing clear processes, tracking progress, and ensuring deliverables meet internal standards, established deadlines, and funder expectations.
- Identify risks and adapt plans to ensure project goals are met in evolving contexts.
- Contribute technical expertise by developing and delivering trainings, providing consultations, and producing written materials aligned with state-identified needs and priority topic areas.
- Cultivate and manage relationships with internal teams and external partners, serving as a point of contact to sustain effective collaboration.
- Support outreach and partnership development for emerging opportunities and assist senior leadership in identifying and pursuing new initiatives.
- Collaborate with the Monitoring & Evaluation team to ensure accurate data collection, analysis, reporting, and documentation of outcomes, lessons learned, and promising practices.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

*Education and Experience*

- Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Social Work, International Affairs, or a related field preferred.
- 3+ years of experience in program or project management.
- Demonstrated experience in assessing and building organizational capacity, monitoring and evaluation, and managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
- Proven ability to liaise effectively with multiple stakeholders, including government agencies (federal, state, and municipal), nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, the business sector, and community groups.
- Strong familiarity with relevant Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded programs and services, with an emphasis on state-administered programming
- Familiarity with grant-funded programming and federal funding requirements

*Skills and Competencies*

- Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
- Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with a track record of effective collaboration across diverse teams.
- Strategic thinker with attention to detail and a solutions-oriented approach.
- Ability to remain calm, flexible, and effective in a fast-paced environment.
- Proficiency in project management tools and Microsoft Office Suite (experience with Airtable preferred).

**Working Environment:** Remote working environment, with potential for travel depending on project needs.

**Compensation:** ($65,000 - $85,000/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international humanitarian organization supporting refugees, internally displaced people and communities affected by displacement. DRC has a long-standing presence in Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, delivering programmes that respond to humanitarian needs while supporting protection, resilience and longer-term solutions for displacement-affected populations.

DRC is moving towards a shared management arrangement across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, bringing the three country operations under a more integrated leadership and management structure while maintaining the appropriate operational and legal arrangements in each country.

 **About the job**

The purpose of the Head of Support Services (HOSS) role is to provide coherent and effective leadership of support functions across the three operations and to enable the new structure to operate efficiently.

The HOSS will lead the development and implementation of harmonized, efficient and fit-for-purpose support services across Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Middle East, Asia and Europe (MEAE) HQ Hub and neighboring country offices where necessary ensuring that systems and resources effectively support programme delivery and organizational priorities. Working closely with the Country Director and senior management, the role will help drive the transition towards shared ways of working, identify opportunities for efficiencies and greater consistency, and ensure strong standards of compliance, risk management and operational support across the three countries and MEAE HQ Hub.

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage Support Services Department Heads across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, including workforce planning, performance, well-being and professional development, while providing technical guidance to the wider support teams.
- Strengthen team capacity through coaching, mentoring, targeted training and regular engagement with country and field offices.
- Promote effective collaboration across the three countries and model DRC’s values, Code of Conduct, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

**Support Services Management**

- Provide strategic leadership and, where required, hands-on support across Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Administration and IT, ensuring responsive, effective and sustainable support to programmes and operations across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq as well as in the MEAE Hub, to best support implementation of strategy
- Strengthen and align support-services systems, processes and controls across the three countries, promoting efficiency and shared approaches where appropriate while responding to different legal, operational and contextual requirements.
- Advise senior management on support-services priorities, compliance, registration, audits, resource management and other operational matters requiring senior-level attention.
- Lead coordinated workforce and resource planning across Finance, Supply Chain, HR, Administration and ICT, ensuring effective financial management and support arrangements across the three countries in line with operational resource plans.
- Ensure effective hosting and operational support to the MEAE HQ Hub, including the support-services arrangements required for Hub staff and functions based in or operating through the three countries.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in the development of the country strategies, annual delivery agreement, and contribute to the strategic leadership of the country programmes.

**Operational Management**

- Lead short- and long-term operational resource planning, ensuring Support Services enable delivery of country strategies, programmes and projects and maintain sufficient capacity to respond to changing operational needs and emergencies.
- Under supervision of the Country Director, oversee implementation of DRC’s Risk Management Framework across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, ensuring robust compliance and internal controls, with country-level mitigation measures managed through the responsibilities set out under Risk Management.
- Ensure relevant policies, standard operating procedures and administrative systems comply with national legislation, donor requirements and DRC organisational standards. In collaboration with the Country Director, lead on managing legal issues and relationships with legal counsel.
- Regularly review and improve Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment is strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Oversee internal and external audits and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions and recommendations, escalating systemic or significant issues to the HQ/ MEAE HQHub as appropriate.
- Contribute to project development, budgeting and resource-allocation decisions and work closely with programme colleagues to ensure Support Services effectively enable programme delivery, localisation and partnerships.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems.Ensure that the country master budget is updated on a regular basis and is used to adequately prepare project proposals to manage resources efficiently.
- Contribute to organisational development initiatives and deputise for the Country Director when formally requested.

**Risk Management**

- Support the Country Director and Senior Management Team in external engagement with donors and authorities on compliance, registration and audit matters.
- As part of the internal and external audit oversight described under Operational Management, supervise audits and controls relating to DRC’s operational standards within Support Services and follow up implementation of corrective actions.
- Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Develop a country risk management plan identifying major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy, linked to the risk register and action plans maintained with Senior Management.
- Participate in audit kick-off and exit meetings and ensure cooperation at all time during every audit field works. Lead on providing management response on each audit report
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure relevant teams across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq use DRC Dynamics effectively and consistently.
- Use system reporting and data to strengthen management oversight, decision-making and operational performance.
- Act as a lead user for relevant Projects and Finance functions and coordinate technical follow-up with the HQ/MEAE HQ Hub where required.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

**Required**

- Minimum 7 years’ relevant experience, including substantial senior-level experience managing Support Services within an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience managing multi-functional Support Services within an INGO with an institutional donor portfolio, including responsibility for donor compliance, financial and operational controls.
- Minimum 4 years’ people-management experience, with proven ability to lead, develop and support diverse teams.
- Strong operational management experience, including in complex and emergency settings, with the ability to provide strategic leadership and hands-on support where required.
- Proactive, solutions-focused and change-oriented leadership style, with the ability and willingness to take the lead, make necessary changes and drive improvements.
- Strong communication, negotiation, planning and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively with country teams, partners, authorities, donors and other stakeholders.

**Desirable**

- Extensive professional experience and strong technical expertise in Finance and/or Supply Chain.
- Knowledge of and ability to manage Microsoft Dynamics 365 ERP is a distinct advantage, particularly across Finance, Supply Chain and related operational functions.

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English required while other proficiency in Arabic is an advantage

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

- A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, or Logistics Management

**We offer**

- Contract length: 12 months contract (Renewable based on funds)
- Band: Management - E1
- Duty Station: Amman – Jordan
- Designation of Duty Station: Unaccompanied – Family Duty Station
- Start date: January 01, 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national and expatriate employees.

title: Coordinator for a Medical Project (Volunteer Coordination & Health Education)
body:
**Med’EqualiTeam** is a French non-profit organization, created in July 2018. Our aim is to provide free health care to displaced populations, who wouldn’t otherwise have access to it due to any kind of barriers or lack of physicians. We are a volunteer based NGO, with most of the staff coming for short period of term in order to support with their medical or translation skills.

We are running since December 2023 a [**project in Northern Greece**](https://www.medequali.team/en/projects/medical-help-thessaloniki/), with mobile medical units reaching out to different centers to provide medical consultations. We also run a Health Education program with first aid trainings and sessions about health topics designed for the community.

## *Job description*

This is a combined role of two coordination branches: Volunteer Coordination & Health Education Coordination.

### **1) Volunteer Coordination**

Are you someone with **great people skills**, **experience in the humanitarian sector**, and a (academic/professional) **background relevant to our medical project** in Thessaloniki e.g., medicine, public health, psychology, social work, etc.?

Then you might be our next *Volunteer Coordinator* managing our volunteer team on the ground in Northern Greece! This role focuses on recruiting qualified volunteers, composing a compatible medical team, supervising volunteer wellbeing, and managing the project’s HR tasks. This role is a great opportunity to gain project management experience in the medical humanitarian field and further hone your leadership skills.

*Job description:*

- Advertise new positions with recruitment partners
- Implement existing processes for recruitment and on-boarding of new (medical) volunteers; registration and evaluation of applications, holding interviews, composing the volunteer team, organising travel and accommodation logistics, conducting volunteer inductions on the ground, conducting check-in and exit chats, etc.
- Gather and implement volunteer feedback
- Coordinate the recruitment and onboarding of community translators
- Organise volunteer schedules in collaboration with the Medical Coordinator and Field Coordinator
- Look out for the wellbeing of volunteers and coordinate wellbeing activities
- Ensure professional behaviour and respect of MET code of conduct by all volunteers
- Ensure the safe storage and confidentiality of all HR data and information according to MET’s processes
- Be the on-site coordinator and manage the reception for approximately 1-2 clinics a week: register patients, coordinate clinic translation and medical volunteers, and manage on-site safety

### **2) Health Education Coordination**

Are you interested in improving the health of asylum seeker and refugee communities through education and empowerment? We are seeking a volunteer with an **interest in training** **and education** to coordinate the health education branch of our medical project in Northern Greece; where we provide first aid training sessions for NGO volunteers and health education sessions to displaced communities across Northern Greece. This role is a great opportunity to develop your coordination and education skills and use your medical experience to deliver preventative health measures.

*Job description:*

- Plan and coordinate first aid trainings and health education sessions with NGO partners across Northern Greece.
- Lead in developing and delivering sessions with support of the medical volunteer team; designing training materials (presentations, leaflets etc.), overseeing translations, conducting focus groups, etc.
- Work with the medical coordinator to shape the strategy of health education and training
- Implement service evaluation protocols by gathering and processing feedback from attendees of sessions to improve the service

*As a key position, we ask for a minimum of **9 months** commitment. The **starting date is 10th of January 2027** with 2 weeks of handover with the current coordinator.*

***This is a volunteer position with a stipend - we cannot facilitate entry into Greece or obtain a visa.***

## ***Required experience and skills***

- Fluency in English
- Minimum time commitment of 6 months
- Strong organizational and administration skills
- Strong communication and reporting skills
- Strong interpersonal and intercultural skills
- A high level of personal organization, flexibility and resilience
- Capable of working independently, while knowing your professional limits and asking for help if needed
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and to MET’s mandate
- A driving licence and experience driving a manual car
- Proficiency on computer (Office pack, PowerPoint, Canva)

## Desired experience and skills

- Experience in HR and in working with volunteers
- Healthcare professional (or student in a health field)
- Previous experience working or volunteering with displaced or vulnerable people
- Previous work experience in NGOs/INGOs
- Experience providing education/training sessions
- Knowledge of locally relevant languages (Greek, Arabic, Farsi, Turkish)

## Benefits of working with Med'EqualiTeam

- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- A highly rewarding and meaningful job
- Work in a multilingual environment
- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- Accommodation in Thessaloniki in a shared flat, transport to the mission site and emergency health insurance provided.
- Please note that this is a voluntary position, which comes with a basic stipend to cover living expenses. Unfortunately, we cannot offer a salary.

title: Area Manager (NES) - Raqqa
body:
About World Vision  
For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.   
Job purpose:

The Area Manager role provides strategic leadership and coordination for operational programming, serving as the principal point of contact for government, UN, and humanitarian stakeholders. The position ensures project alignment with organizational strategy, navigates complex regulatory environments, and maintains operational access and compliance. The post holder is expected to lead on the development, planning, implementation, and monitoring of programming in Northeast Syria (NES), working closely across all departments, including Technical Advisors, Grant Acquisition and Management, Finance, People and Culture, Partnerships, Security, and Program Support, to achieve high-quality results and operational excellence. The post holder is also in charge of positioning and strengthening WVSR’s engagement with governmental entities and key stakeholders in NES, ensuring an informed operational presence, and supporting the expansion and integration of program operations, as well as supporting the R&C department in registration as needed. The position will report to the Deputy Director of Field Operations.

Major Responsibilities:  
PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT 30%  
• Ensure that the portfolio of projects has sectoral alignment per the Syria Response strategy.  
• Ensure assigned projects are properly planned and implemented to meet  
• agreed results, timelines, and budget indicators.  
• Ensure that assigned projects are adequately staffed to facilitate effective implementation.   
• Facilitate reporting on the progress of field implementation.   
• Analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of field implementation and introduce corrective measures where needed (key focus on managing burn rates).   
• Ensure proper implementation of projects (financially and programmatically) according to WVSR standards throughout the life of the Project Cycle Management   
• In collaboration with the Partnerships Manager, identify areas for staff/partner development   
• Engage with partners constructively to facilitate effective partnerships on projects under the portfolio.

PROJECT PLANNING AND DESIGN 25%   
• Work closely with Technical Advisors and GAM on planning and designing new proposal log frames   
• Lead /support respective Project Managers in developing the project budget (DPC) during the design process

STAFF MANAGEMENT 25%   
• Determine staffing requirements and facilitate hiring and orientation.   
• Facilitate staff training and development.   
• Set objectives for staff, monitor their performance and provide feedback.   
• Ensure staff wellbeing.

LIAISON and COORDINATION 10%   
• Represent World Vision Syria Response (WVSR) in NES and engage with local authorities, administrative bodies, and coordination platforms to ensure smooth operational access and compliance.   
• Act as WVSR's representative in Area Coordination Groups at the sub national level, aligned with the Syria NGO Forum and UN Hubs in NES.   
• Participate in relevant meetings, conferences, and cluster coordination forums by authorities, organized by authorities, UN agencies, and humanitarian actors.   
• Lead high-level discussions with security forces, local councils, and government entities to facilitate approvals, resolve access issues, and maintain operational continuity.   
• Prepare and submit quarterly and annual reports, project reports for each project, ensuring they are signed and stamped by relevant authorities in accordance with NES legal regulations.   
• Oversee and initiate the formal registration process for WVSR with authorities yearly, ensuring compliance with local governance requirements.   
• Prepare and manage all Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) between WVSR and authorities, ensuring all agreements are finalized for the project start-up.   
• Ensure all correspondence with authorities adheres to WVSR policies and is documented, retained, and filed in an organized and secure manner.   
• Work with authorities to secure all required authorizations and permissions for local staff movement and distributions, for project implementation, and facilitate international staff to move and cross the WVI NES office.   
• Coordinate with WVSR partners to ensure proper representation of WVSR in all official documentation, including permits, MoUs, and annual reports.   
• Submit regular liaison activity reports, including updates on permits, meetings held, challenges encountered, and strategic recommendations.   
• Maintain a clear record of all liaison engagements, decisions, and agreements to institutional support to support institutional memory and accountability.   
INTERNAL PROCESSES SUPPORT 10%   
• Support the Deputy Director of Field Operations with correctly implementing established internal processes.   
• Raise and highlight any discrepancies or malfunctions of internal process • design vis-à-vis the correct implementation.  
• Support the revision and correction of internal processes within WVSR in coordination with other departmental functions.

Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role.

1\. Required Professional Experience   
\- A minimum of 8 years of humanitarian and development experience in North East Syria.   
\- Experience designing and implementing multi-sector humanitarian programs   
\- Experience managing and overseeing budgets of at least $3M   
\- Experience working across multiple internal departments, convening and leading people.   
\- Experience with remote management and partner management   
\- Strong communication skills with the ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively (oral and written) with senior members of the humanitarian community as well as with field practitioners.   
\- Knowledge of computer software such as MS Office and email programs.

2\. Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:   
\- Post Graduate University degree in International Development or other related majors OR significant humanitarian leadership experience in lieu of formal education requirements.

3\. Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications   
\- Comprehensive knowledge of International Human Rights Law, International Humanitarian Law, Refugee Law, the relevant positions of the UN, ICRC, and major NGOs on protection of civilians, in particular of IDPs, women, and children, the codes of conduct, the Humanitarian Charter, The Sphere Project, etc.   
\- Detail-oriented, with demonstrated experience in follow-up and ensuring complex ideas turn into action.   
\- Concrete, practical hands-on experience in remote management aid delivery contexts.   
\- Strong knowledge of key sectoral areas, including programmatic approaches to health and protection programming.   
\- Experienced and confident in external representation with donors and within formal and informal coordination structures   
\- Highly developed communication skills (oral and written) with the ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively with senior internal and external stakeholders.   
\- Demonstrated success as a collaborator and team builder committed to the transfer of knowledge.   
\- Ability to work effectively under pressure.   
\- Innovator and calculated risk taker.   
\- Understands, values, and promotes diversity to achieve organizational goals.   
\- Experience designing and implementing programs in Syria, through partners, is highly preferred.   
\- Full adherence to World Vision Child Protection, Code of Conduct, and Conflict of Interest policies.   
\- Experience in establishing, designing, and implementing cross-border programs through partners is highly preferred.

4\. Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement   
\- willingness to travel domestically around NES and internationally up to 20% of the time.

5\. Language Requirements   
\- Essential: Strong English and Arabic

title: Durable Solutions Programme Development Manager Somalia (Open for Somali Nationals only)
body:
**Background:**

Displacement in Somalia remains a complex and protracted challenge affecting millions of displaced people and returning refugees. NRC responds through integrated, multi-sectoral and area-based approaches that not only meet immediate needs but address systemic barriers preventing displaced people from progressing towards durable solutions. This response is also closely aligned with influencing and enabling the implementation of policies that promote greater inclusion and rights of displacement affected communities in both countries. The Durable Solutions (DS) Programme Manager provides strategic leadership and technical expertise, coordinates funding and partnerships, engages key stakeholders, and supports policy and advocacy efforts to achieve sustainable outcomes for displacement-affected communities.

**What you will do:**

The overall purpose of the Durable Solutions (DS) Programme Manager position is to lead and oversee the implementation of NRC's Durable Solutions programming in Somalia. The position provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and managerial oversight to ensure the effective delivery, quality, and growth of the Durable Solutions portfolio. The DS programme manager may also provide support to NRC Kenya programme on ad-hoc basis.

The DS Programme Manager is responsible for managing and strengthening the capacity of programme teams, providing strategic direction and technical guidance on the design and implementation of DS programming, ensuring the development of timely, high-quality proposals, reports, and programme documentation, and maintaining compliance with NRC standards and donor requirements. The role also represents NRC externally, builds and sustains strategic partnerships with key stakeholders and coordination fora, and coordinates resource mobilization efforts to support the expansion and sustainability of the Durable Solutions portfolio.

General Responsibilities:

1. To be responsible for providing technical support to colleagues working on DS programmes and develop relevant DS training including coaching of newly recruited staff to ensure they meet NRC’s standards. Also contribute to the induction of new staff with a role in the DS project implementation processes.
2. Assume overall responsibility of coordinating and managing the DS programme design and implementation (activities, budget and project documentation) in line with proposals, strategies and donor requirements.
3. Responsible for Overall backstopping of DS program staff to ensure integrated and area-based programming is realized within NRC DS operation areas and closely support and coordinate DS programmes.
4. Compliance to donor standards, and grant management and regular reporting to donor in Country Office
5. Ensure compliance with contractual commitments and extracting, documenting and implementing key learnings from project implementation

Specific responsibilities:

- Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all new and existing projects and activities within the Country Durable Solutions portfolio throughout the project cycle, ensuring project design, start-up, implementation, monitoring, and close-out are aligned with NRC quality standards and donor requirements.
- Work with NRC Country and Area Programme teams, including CC Specialists, Managers, and Coordinators, both remotely and on-site, to develop and apply context-specific technical solutions for Durable Solutions programming, policy influence and strategic planning.
- Support the application of standards, best practices, partnership approaches, programme tools, and MEAL systems to ensure high-quality programme implementation and evidence-based decision-making.
- Lead programme learning, information management, research, and evidence-generation initiatives, identifying opportunities for learning and innovation and facilitating the documentation and dissemination of lessons learned and good practices.
- Promote the integration of innovations, best practices, and programme learning into programme design, implementation, and strategic decision-making to improve programme quality and impact.

**Please read the** [**full Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDmGBbZc4zTQpPhkkfE_P5eAX8p5o8IeXlZ_3VZEPXnxsc?e=jkF1j6) **as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Minimum first level university degree in Development Economics, Social Sciences or other relevant fields.
- Demonstrated flexibility and the ability to work under pressure in a complex and changing environment.
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts
- Knowledge of the displacement context(s) in Somalia
- Experience with returns and reintegration programmes
- Documented results in project and program management
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal
- Resilient, with the ability to live and work in a complex, insecure and challenging context.

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Minimum of 5 years’ experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- In-depth knowledge of the main protection and humanitarian standards and legal frameworks.
- Significant work experience in INGOs or UN in assisting IDPs, refugees and returnees with a focus on durable solutions.
- Clear understanding of durable solutions, self-reliance, and related concepts, and experience designing and implementing integrated approaches which effectively advance them.
- Experience in ensuring programming aligns with and contributes to inclusive policy implementation.
- Experience in building strong coalitions and strong networks and designing programs and resource mobilization for multi-year programs in an international environment.
- Solid budgeting skills and understanding of working with multiple donors including FCDO, EU, WB, SIDA, DANIDA, and others.
- Strong experience working in a partnership model and establishing and maintaining coordination and communication systems at inter-agency level
- Knowledge of the context in Somalia and Horn of Africa in general.
- Experience with start-up, exit or similar

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Any of the NRC’s area offices (Mogadishu, Kismayo, Galkayo or Hargeisa) **(national contract)**
- Contract: Fixed Term **national contact.**
- Travel: *50%*
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **national** salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Somalia. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency permits.
- **If the internal pool is competitive, NRC will prioritize the assessment of internal staff before reviewing applications from external candidates.**
- **Qualified female candidates are particularly encouraged to apply.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Assist with housing set-ups for new arrivals as needed.
- Assist clients in completing initial medical appointments as needed.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $186 per month, dental starting at $9.00 per month, and vision starting at $4 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:** ($20.97$). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

 **Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Country Director, Yemen
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than twenty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

The IRC launched an emergency health response in Yemen in 2012. Since then, and despite continued instability and conflict, the IRC has extended its presence throughout the country, implementing a diverse, integrated program of health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and cash programs. These programs prioritize local partnerships with both public institutions and civil society, and span emergency response, humanitarian, and recovery modalities, while serving vulnerable Yemenis including IDPs and returnees, migrants and refugees, women, children, and youth.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director (CD) sets the strategic direction, leads all programs, emergency response, financial and operational matters, and oversees humanitarian access and the adherence to and application of security measures, as well as external relationships and partnerships in Yemen. As lead of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the CD ensures accountability of the SMT for the overall leadership and supervisory management of approximately 120 IRC staff and more than 400 incentive workers, programming, and operations, including program quality and accountability, stewardship of resources, staff safety and security, performance management, and external representation, for which the CD remains accountable.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary, demonstrated leadership abilities who deploys strong communication and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong contextual analytical skills and an ability to translate the impact of geopolitical developments and rapidly changing humanitarian conditions into operational priorities and effective responses. They will build a network of partnerships, diversify program resources, and ensure organizational readiness to respond to emerging and escalating emergencies while maintaining continuity of critical humanitarian services. They will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design, and deliver responsive, high-quality humanitarian, emergency response, early recovery, and development programs; ensuring the efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance, and focused, timely reporting; and overseeing financial management and compliance systems.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Lead the country program by maintaining open and professional relations with colleagues, promoting a strong team spirit, and providing guidance, oversight, and resources to enable staff to perform successfully.
- Lead strategic representation and positioning with national and local authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private), European Union; UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups. Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Play a leadership role in efforts to improve humanitarian response coordination in Yemen
- Provide leadership for strong, mutually beneficial, and effective partnerships with Yemeni organizations.
- Seek out and pursue respectful and safe opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Yemen, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.
- Lead country program collaboration with colleagues in the IRC’s MENAU region to deliver regional programming and advocacy.
- Ensure leadership and management processes enable the IRC to effectively adapt to contextual changes and fully leverage opportunities to expand humanitarian access and assistance.
- Collaborate closely with regional leadership and neighboring country programs to address cross-border and regional issues coherently and effectively.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Growth***

- Set the strategic vision and direction of the country program is aligned with IRC’s strategy to serve more people with the most responsive and highest quality programming possible and secure the resources necessary to do so.
- Ensure the strategy action plan is of quality, implemented and guides decision making, to achieve IRC’s ambitions in Yemen and contribute to IRC’s strategic objectives globally.
- Ensure program quality through consistent use throughout the country program of rigorous assessment, design, and proposal development and review processes; comprehensive monitoring & evaluation, accountability and learning systems; staff development investments; and partner organization capacity strengthening.
- Actively seek out and pursue opportunities to expand, in line with the IRC’s mission, humanitarian, resilience and development programming in Yemen, in terms of populations and areas served.
- Develop a deep understanding of the geopolitical landscape and remain current on context analysis and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure timely submission of competitive, responsive, and high-quality proposals, and support colleagues in negotiations with donors.
- Lead implementation of IRC’s objective of expanding partnerships with Yemeni civil society organizations, and ensuring strong collaborative, principled partnerships that deliver effective and efficient program outcomes.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to changing contexts.
- Ensure the SMT delivers the leadership, management structures, staffing skills and approaches, and operational systems required to ensure a coherent “one IRC” approach to achieve Yemen and regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities for appropriate expansion and growth of programs, supported by the acquisition and investment of human resources.

***Emergency Response Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall strategic and operational emergency response readiness and action for the country program.
- Lead Country Context Analysis, Emergency Response Planning and Strategy Development as well as In-Country Emergency Response Teams
- Ensure the country program maintains robust emergency preparedness and response capacity, including crisis management structures, clear decision-making protocols, and surge readiness to enable rapid operational scale-up or adaptation in volatile contexts.
- Lead and oversee the management timely, well-coordinated, and principled responses to emergencies, including conflict escalation, displacements, critical incidents, and program disruptions.
- Engage with Regional and Global Emergency Response Teams prior to, during and post emergency response, in line with organizational Emergency Guidelines.
- Represent IRC with peer organizations, and other emergency response agencies operating in Yemen.
- Ensure coordinated emergency response in the event of cross-border/regional emergencies.

***Safety and Security Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Lead and oversee the management of all security risks and incidents, ensure timely, well-coordinated, and ensure primacy of the wellbeing and security of our clients, staff and partners. Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including training and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation, and contingency plans current and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety and Security Director on safety and security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.
- Liaise with the regional office, with peer agencies and use the tools and information portals available to keep abreast of all security-related matters; In case of necessity, ensure adequate roll-out of emergency procedures.

***Staff Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives and providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide direct oversight and guidance to multi-disciplinary teams across cross-cultural settings, ensuring performance excellence and alignment with strategic objectives.
- Effectively manage staff across various functions and locations, including setting clear expectations, performance monitoring, and accountability frameworks.
- Lead sensitive and complex staff-related conversations (e.g., performance issues, conflict resolution) with professionalism, empathy, and respect.
- Mentor and coach high-potential staff to support career progression and leadership development within the organization.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing across teams and departments.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to deliver compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, especially in the areas of People and Culture, finance, and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Yemen country program’s financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for grant funds and discretionary funds.
- Ensure a country-wide culture of safeguarding, grounded in accountability, transparency, and survivor-centered response. Provide strategic leadership to mainstream safeguarding across all country program operations and partnerships, in line with IRC’s Safeguarding Policy.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Regional Vice President - MENAU

**Position directly Supervises:** A senior management team responsible for Programs, Operations, Finance, People and Culture, Field Management, and Safety & Security and Compliance and Risk Management.

**Key Internal Contacts:** Country Program: All staff, Region: MENAU Regional Team, Head Office: Crisis Response and Recovery Department (CRRD), Ethics & Compliance, Operations and Strategy, Finance, Global Philanthropy & Partnerships, Technical Excellence and General Counsel.

**Key External Contacts:** Partner organizations, host country government officials, public and private donor agencies, international and national NGOs, UN agencies

**PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:**

- Strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and ability to deploy strong communications effectively, both internally and externally, and in emergency operational contexts. Ability to build networks, partnerships and diversify program resources.
- Experience in a leadership role in conflict settings and situations of constrained humanitarian access required.
- Graduate degree in a relevant field.
- At least 12 years of dynamically responsible international work experience, including leadership at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment, with demonstrated responsibility for emergency preparedness, crisis management, and operational response. Preference for experience in the MENAU Region.
- Fluency in English is required. Arabic is a preferred asset.

**Demonstrated Technical Skills:**

- Superior communication skills, verbal and written.
- Experience in managing security in a complex and rapidly changing security context.
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with both institutional and private donors.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Prior work experience and a keen understanding of political complexities in Yemen and the Middle East and North Africa region is preferred.

**Demonstrated Managerial/Leadership Competencies:**

- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in cross-cultural settings, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Analytical, strategic, and able to proactively develop solutions to complex challenges.
- Comfortable with ambiguity and decision making in a fast-paced environment.
- Effective in developing high-potential staff to achieve career growth and maximum contribution.
- Proven experience in managing high-quality programming that meets the needs of clients.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels of oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Experience building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization.
- Opportunity-awareness. A successful innovative approach to unpredictable programming, operational, and funding contexts.
- Ability to dispassionately represent program context, constraints, and successes to media, government, and other senior audiences.
- Highly resilient and comfortable working in an insecure environment with restricted personal freedoms.

**Ability to Travel: Position is primarily based in Aden, Yemen.** Approximately 5-10 % outside the region for workshops, representation, and conferences.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and giving them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENAU, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Executive Director
body:
ICVA is looking for an Executive Director to harness the power of its large global membership and lead its secretariat to see the 2030 Strategy through to its close and shape what comes next.

## **About ICVA**

Founded in 1962, the International Council of Voluntary Agencies (ICVA) is a global network of NGOs. Our mission is to make humanitarian action more principled and effective by working collectively and independently to influence policy and practice.

Our members range from local and national organisations to large international NGOs. Working together, the Secretariat leads the network across three areas: Forced Displacement, Humanitarian Coordination and Humanitarian Financing, with the promotion of humanitarian principles running through all areas of work.

The secretariat is based in Geneva, with regional representation across Middle East, Asia Pacific, West, Central and East Africa and Latin America.

### **Managing the Secretariat**

The Executive Director heads a dispersed secretariat team, headquartered in Geneva, with staff currently in Amman, Bangkok, Bogota, Dublin, Nairobi, and Yaoundé. Yet leading ICVA is more than running an organisation. The secretariat exists to convene, support and amplify its members, so much of the Executive Director's leadership is exercised through influence, trust, and consensus.

Success depends on multiple factors: ensuring a well managed effective and funded secretariat, building a strong team, working under pressure in a constrained resource environment; listening to members across regions, bringing differing views to common ground and making sure the network as a whole is present in the decisions that affect humanitarian action and representing the vision of the members at Principal level in senior policy fora.

## **Why the network matters**

ICVA's value lies in both its members services, providing the members with tools, information, collective platforms and partnership, networking opportunities to facilitate their work and doing what members could not do alone, representing the collective NGO vision to forge an effective humanitarian system. The network brings the experience of NGOs working alongside people affected by crisis into the places where humanitarian policy is decided and carries those decisions back to the organisations that put them into practice.

It is also a space where NGOs of very different sizes, origins and mandates can test ideas, agree common positions and speak with one voice. That collective voice carries more weight with UN agencies, member states and donors than any single organisation could achieve on its own.

## **Influential Representation**

ICVA holds a number of representative roles on behalf of the NGO community. The Executive Director represents the network among the Principals of the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC), the most senior forum for international humanitarian coordination with the UN system, where ICVA is one of three NGO consortia invited on a permanent basis.

The Secretariat hosts key initiatives in the humanitarian sector - including the CBPF Resource Facility, the newly launched NRG Facility under the Grand Bargain, the Interagency PSEA Community Outreach and Communication Fund and is currently serving as PSEA Champion.

These roles carry real responsibility. In them, the Executive Director speaks for a diverse membership, and must earn and keep the trust of members, member states, UN and other international agencies and donors alike.

### **Shaping the next strategic period**

ICVA is nearing the close of its 2030 Strategy. With three years of the current strategy still to run, the incoming Executive Director will see it through to completion while leading the development of the new strategic plan that will underpin the next phase for ICVA.

That means taking stock with members of what has been achieved, reading a changing humanitarian landscape, and working with the Board to set a direction that keeps ICVA relevant and useful to the organisations it exists to serve.

## **Purpose of the role**

Working closely with Board members and reporting the Board Chair, the ED will lead the development and implementation of ICVA's strategy, oversee its financial and operational performance, and strengthen fundraising and partnerships. The ED will provide strong an effective leadership for the Secretariat Team.

The ED will represent an influential global network of civil society members, working with the members, partners and governmental bodies.
