The ED will be responsible for the further development of the ICVA network by building on its strengths, maintaining the confidence of its Members, donors and stakeholders, and ensuring that ICVA delivers measurable, sustainable, and demonstrable impact for people affected by crisis.

For full details of the role please refer to: [https://icvanetwork.org/opportunities/7575](https://icvanetwork.org/opportunities/7575)

title: SOUTH SUDAN - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIPS HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - JUBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location : Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The Grants department currently has 1 Grants & Partnership Head of Department Expat, 1 Grants Manager Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer National. With the mission scale up, the idea is to add Compliance Manager National. A Compliance coordinator supports the mission only part time and is therefore not in charge of audits.

## About the job

**General objective:**

\- The objectives of the position rely on donor engagement, financing and partnership strategy, preparation of project documents, contract management, partnership management, compliance and external audits, external communication, internal control.  
\- Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Grants & Partnership Head of Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. He/She supervises, adapts and optimises working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.  
The Grants Department validates contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.  
It plays a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). The Grants & Partnership Head of Department ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- SI has increased the number of consortium we lead/are part of and we need the Grants department to support better engagement with these partners.  
\- SI also needs to have more capacities to engage on the localization agenda.  
\- In the meantime, SI needs to build a strong Grants department supported by national staffs.  
\- The Grants & Partnership Department scale up should facilitate and lighten the work of the program teams on the ground who have to face an increasing number of reporting & proposal requests.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\- Support localization effort and engage with a couple of selected local partners.  
\- Support follow up of proposals submitted in the Dec-Jan period (notably ECHO)

**Security constraints :**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.  
The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves  
There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.  
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).  
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master Degree in financial / accountancy studies

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experience on a similar position : 0-2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Excellent writing skills & mastering of MS Office suite

2\. Donors rule understanding & knowledge: ECHO, CDCS, FIFSAN, Norway MoFA, FCDO, DoS, SSHF

3\. Donor platform technicities: APPEL, GMS, UNPP

4\. Contractual management

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Capacity building experience

2\. Department structuring knowledge

3\. Information management structuration is a +

4\. Networking capacities

5\. Very hands-on: not top senior management only: capacity to be a doer as well

6\. Attraction for the field

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Very good in English, written and spoken.

2\. French & Arabic are a +

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**   
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grants & Parternships Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.  
Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.  
Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors and has been one of the first responders of the cholera

response.

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Malakal and a sub-office in Renk. The field office in Renk has been set-up to support the ongoing response to the Sudan Crisis and to ensure constant monitoring and rapid access to

affected communities. SI's long term presence in Upper Nile enables the organization to ensure proper coordination with other key players on the ground in order to provide a high-quality response and avoid duplication of

efforts. The response has focused on cholera since November 2024 while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- SI has recently closed its operations in Unity but is looking at starting interventions in Northern Bahr-El-Ghazal (Aweil): base opening planned for spring 2025.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2025, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 5+ million, and there are 70+ employees. This is the result of a scale-down following US funding cut in 2025 that are finally relaunched.

The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The Finance Deprtement is: Finance Coordinator Expatriate + 1 Chief Accountant + 1 Finance Assistant

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Deputy Head of Finance supports the Head of Finance in the overall financial management of the mission and ensures the implementation of SI financial procedures.

He/she assists the Finance Coordinator in preparing budget proposals, ensuring financial reporting complies with donor requirements, and updating the monthly budget follow-up. He/she also validates coordination expenses and ensures costs are allocated in accordance with the agreed cost-allocation methodology.

He/she supervises the Chief Accountant at the coordination level and provides technical guidance and support to the mission’s Finance Team. In the absence of the Finance Coordinator, he/she assumes delegated responsibilities to ensure continuity of finance operations.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

-Train and support the newly recruited National Deputy Head of Finance.

-Clear the accounting backlog resulting from the Deputy Head of Finance vacancy.

-Support the Finance Coordinator in managing shared cost allocations.

-Assist the Finance Coordinator in preparing budget proposals.

**Security constraints:**

Juba remains a volatile security context

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master degree in Finance

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 0/2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Similar Experience

2\. Knowledge about the accounting Software

3\. Budget Management and Financial Reporting Experience

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Clear Communication

2\. Autonomy

3\. Problem Solving

**LANGUAGES**

1\. English

2\. Arabic (Juba)

## SI will offer you...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR XXX gross per month (2250 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

"The Deputy Finance Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and

title: Mental Health Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTION:**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad. Assistance to Sudanese refugees expanded to include the management of eleven camps in the east and one camp in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, IRC expanded its geographic coverage to Guéra Province, where the organization currently works in five health districts and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population, as well as family planning, response, and prevention activities related to gender-based violence (GBV). In May 2016, IRC established a presence in Lac Province to respond to the crisis caused by Boko Haram. In its 2022–2024 Strategic Action Plan, IRC Chad is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and line ministries in key sectors to ensure that IRC’s actions are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the initiatives undertaken.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Senior Health Coordinator, the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist based in Hadjer Hadid will be responsible for the overall management and implementation of a high-quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) program in all of IRC’s areas of operation, and more specifically in refugee camps. The Mental Health Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Public Health’s mental health program, UNHCR, IRC, HIAS, and all members of the mental health working group in Chad to facilitate the coordination of mental health interventions in the country and strengthen their integration into the minimum package of services provided in health centers and hospitals. The mental health and psychosocial support specialist will supervise health workers in providing prevention, diagnosis, and treatment services for patients with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, using the guidelines of the WHO/UNHCR Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP), and will train new providers on the mhGAP model. She/he will develop standard operating procedures for providing psychological support and psychiatric care, as well as psychosocial support through group psychoeducation and community-based programs. She/he will represent IRC at all mental health working group meetings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Program Coordination:
- Coordinate mental health needs assessments;
- Organize regular meetings on mental health with health program managers and the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) team, in collaboration with other technical coordinators;
- Ensure that mental health and psychosocial support are fully integrated into the various sectors of the health program (primary health care, sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, environmental health) and other IRC programs (WPE and ERD);
- Coordinate the implementation of all interventions in the field of mental health and psychosocial support
- Contribute to capacity building for the MHPSS team to enable them to effectively carry out their duties and ensure a smooth transition;
- Participate in capacity building for local partners (Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, United Nations agencies, etc.) in the field of mental health and psychosocial support;
- Contribute to the development of new funding proposals for mental health and psychosocial support;

**Evaluation and Monitoring of the Quality of Clinical and Community Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services**

- Conduct a situational analysis to identify and assess mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) needs in IRC’s areas of operation in Chad
- Provide formative supervision and/or refresher training for healthcare providers and community health workers.
- Provide specialized mental health consultations and psychosocial support to people with specific needs, including survivors of gender-based violence
- Support the organization of community-based services to improve care, follow-up, and referrals between the community and health facilities.
- Conduct formative supervision of health workers to improve the quality of mental health services provided in health facilities and the community using IRC supervision checklists.
- Ensure that essential medicines and psychotropic drugs approved by the Ministry of Public Health (MSP)/WHO are available in health facilities and that they are properly stored and prescribed by providers.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Reporting**

- In collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator, conduct a monthly analysis of mental health and psychosocial support data and share the database and report with the Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribute to improving the quality of periodic health program reports and donor reports.
- Support the monitoring and evaluation framework for the mental health program through regular data analysis and supervision of program activities in the field;
- Document lessons learned, innovative approaches, and the generation of information and evidence to contribute to IRC’s overall learning;
- Work with the MEAL Coordinator and program managers to ensure that health data collection systems meet the requirements of IRC, the Ministry of Public Health (MSP), and donors

**Partnership, Coordination, and Representation**

- Represent IRC at meetings with partners from the Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, and United Nations agencies working in the mental health and psychosocial support sector
- Participate in the development of the mental health working group’s roadmap
- Provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Health in the development and review of national policies, guidelines, standards, protocols, and programs/modules.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Direct Supervisor: Senior Health Coordinator
- Positions under direct supervision: Mental Health Manager in MIP with the Medical Doctor responsible for the health program
- Indirect supervision: Deputy Director of Programs
- Internal: Communications, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & Logistics Departments
- External: Government partners, humanitarian NGOs, and United Nations agencies

**Job requirements:**

- Advanced degree in clinical mental health, preferably a medical degree with a specialty in psychiatry and experience in neurology;
- Three years of professional experience in the development and management of mental health and psychosocial support programs, preferably in emergency situations or refugee camps;
- In addition to the clinical degree, an additional degree in public health is preferred.
- Knowledge of and experience applying the IASC MHPSS guidelines and best practices as part of previous professional experience.
- Experience in assessment, program design, technical training, and supervision using the WHO’s Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP).
- Flexibility in work;
- Ability to work independently while also being an excellent team leader;
- Technical expertise in program development and in assessing and facilitating training needs;
- Strong organizational and supervisory skills.
- Strong analytical skills demonstrating an understanding of current concepts, priorities, and issues related to monitoring, data collection, and program evaluation;
- Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work in a multicultural environment;
- Fluency in French is required; fluency in English is a plus.

**Work Environment:**

**Security:** He or she will be based in Hadjer Hadid and will travel frequently to IRC’s areas of operation. This is an unaccompanied position.

**Gender Equality**: The IRC is committed to reducing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that enable women to participate in the workforce, including parental leave, safety protocols that take into account the specific needs of men and women, and other supportive benefits and allowances.  
  
**The IRC is an equal opportunity employer**. The IRC evaluates all candidates based on merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

**French Version:**

**DESCRIPTION :**

IRC a commencé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire causée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour à l’est du Tchad. L'assistance aux réfugiés soudanais s’est étendue à la gestion de onze camps dans l'Est et d'un camp dans l'Ouest en apportant un appui aux réfugiés et aux communautés locales en matière de santé, nutrition et eau, hygiène et assainissement. En 2012, IRC a étendu sa couverture géographique dans la province du Guéra où l’organisation travaille actuellement dans cinq districts sanitaires et fournit des services de prévention et de traitement de la malnutrition à la population locale ainsi que des activités de planification familiale, de prévention des violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et de réponse à celles-ci. En mai 2016, IRC a établi sa présence dans la province du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram. L’IRC Tchad s'engage dans son plan d'action stratégique 2022-2024 à continuer à fournir des services humanitaires essentiels en santé, nutrition et protection / VBG, tout en améliorant le bien-être économique et en renforçant la résilience des bénéficiaires, en particulier des femmes et des filles. L’IRC Tchad continuera à travailler avec et à soutenir étroitement les acteurs étatiques / ministères sectoriels des domaines clés afin que les actions de l'IRC s'intègrent dans les politiques nationales pour assurer une meilleure appropriation des actions entreprises.

**Description du poste:**

Sous la supervision directe du Senior Health Coordinator, le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial basé à Hadjer Hadid sera responsable de la gestion globale et de la mise en œuvre du programme de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (SMSPS) de qualité dans toutes les zones d’intervention d’IRC et plus spécifiquement dans les camps de réfugiés. Le spécialiste en santé mentale travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le programme de santé mentale du ministère de la Santé publique (MSP), le HCR, l'IRC, HIAS et tous les membres du groupe de travail en santé mentale au Tchad afin de faciliter la coordination des interventions en santé mentale dans le pays et renforcer leur intégration dans le paquet minimum des activités fournies dans les centres de santé et les hôpitaux. Le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial supervisera les agents de santé dans la fourniture des services de prévention, de diagnostic et de traitement des patients souffrant de troubles mentaux, neurologiques et de toxicomanie en utilisant les directives du programme d'action pour les lacunes en matière de santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS / HCR et formera de nouveaux prestataires sur le modèle mhGAP. Elle / il développera des procédures opérationnelles standard pour la fourniture d'un soutien psychologique et de soins psychiatriques, ainsi qu’un soutien psychosocial par le biais de la psychoéducation de groupe et de programmes communautaires. Elle /Il représentera IRC dans toutes les réunions du groupe de travail en santé mentale.

**Responsabilités principales :**

**Coordination de programme :**

- Coordonner les évaluations des besoins en santé mentale ;
- Organiser des réunions régulières sur la santé mentale avec les gestionnaires du programme santé et l’équipe SMSPS en collaboration avec les autres coordinateurs techniques ;
- S’assurer que la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial sont pleinement intégrés aux différents secteurs du programme santé (santé primaire, santé sexuelle et reproductive, nutrition, santé environnementale) et aux autres programmes de l’IRC (WPE et ERD) ;
- Coordonner la mise en œuvre de toutes les interventions dans le domaine de la SMSPS
- Contribuer au renforcement des capacités de l’équipe SMSPS pour leur permettre d’assurer efficacement leurs fonctions et d’assurer la relève ;
- Participer au renforcement des capacités des partenaires locaux (MSP, ONG, agences des Nations Unies, etc.) dans le domaine de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial.
- Contribuer à l’élaboration de nouvelles propositions de financement en santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial;

**Évaluation et suivi de la qualité des services cliniques et communautaires de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial**

- Mener une analyse de la situation afin d'identifier et d'évaluer les besoins en SMSPS dans les zones d’intervention de IRC au Tchad
- Réaliser des supervisions formatives et/ou des recyclages à l’intention des prestataires de soins et des agents de santé communautaires.
- Réaliser les consultations spécialisées en santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial des personnes ayant des besoins spécifiques, y compris les survivants des VBG
- Apporter un appui à l’organisation de l’offre des services communautaires pour une meilleure prise en charge, le suivi et le référencement entre la communauté et les établissements de santé.
- Réaliser les supervisions formatives des agents de santé afin d’améliorer la qualité de services de santé mentale fournis dans les établissements de santé et la communauté à l'aide des listes de contrôle de supervision d’IRC.
- S’assurer que les médicaments essentiels et les psychotropes approuvés par le MSP/OMS sont disponibles dans les établissements de santé et qu’ils sont correctement stockés et prescrits par les prestataires.

**Suivi, évaluation, recherche, apprentissage et rapportage**

- En collaboration avec le Coordinateur MEAL, faire une analyse mensuelle des données de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial et partager la base des données et le rapport avec le Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration de la qualité des rapports périodiques du programme santé et des rapports bailleurs.
- Soutenir le dispositif de suivi et évaluation appliqué au programme de santé mentale à travers des analyses régulières des données et la supervision des activités du programme sur le terrain ;
- Documenter les leçons apprises, les approches innovantes et la production d’informations et de données probantes afin de participer à l’apprentissage global d’IRC ;
- Travailler avec le Coordinateur MEAL et les responsables du programme afin de s’assurer que les systèmes de collecte des données santé remplissent les exigences d’IRC, du MSP et des bailleurs.

**Partenariat, Coordination et Représentation**

- Représenter IRC aux réunions avec les partenaires du ministère de la santé, les ONG et les agences des Nations Unies qui interviennent dans le secteur de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial
- Participer à l’élaboration de la feuille de route du groupe de travail en santé mentale
- Apporter une assistance technique au MSP dans l’élaboration et l’examen des politiques, directives, normes, protocoles, programmes/modules nationaux.

**Principales relations de travail:**

- **Superviseur Hiérarchique :** Senior Health Coordinator  
    **Position sous supervision directe :** Manager Santé Mentale en MIP avec le Médecin responsable du programme santé
- **Supervision indirecte:** Directeur adjoint des Programmes
- **Internes :** Département de communication, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & logistique
- **Externes** *:* Les partenaires de l’État, ONG humanitaires & Agences des Nations Unies

**Exigences du poste:**

- Diplôme supérieur en santé mentale clinique, de préférence un diplôme de médecin avec une spécialisation en psychiatrie et une expérience en neurologie ;
- Trois années d'expérience professionnelle dans le développement et la gestion de programmes de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial, de préférence dans les situations d'urgence ou dans des camps de réfugiés ;
- En plus du diplôme clinique, un diplôme supplémentaire en santé publique est préférable.
- Connaissance et expérience d’application des directives et des bonnes pratiques de l’IASC en matière de SMSPS dans le cadre de son expérience professionnelle antérieure.
- Expérience de l'évaluation, de la conception de programmes, de la formation technique et de la supervision à l'aide du programme d'action contre les lacunes en santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS.
- Flexibilité dans le travail ;
- Capacité à travailler de manière autonome tout en étant un excellent chef d'équipe ;
- Une expertise technique dans l’élaboration de programme et dans l’évaluation et facilitation des besoins en formation ;
- Solides compétences en matière d'organisation et de supervision.
- Solides capacités d’analyse démontrant une compréhension des concepts, priorités et problèmes actuels en matière de suivi, de collecte de données et d'évaluation de programmes.
- Solides compétences interpersonnelles et capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel.
- La maîtrise de la langue française est requise ; la maîtrise de l'anglais est un atout.

**Environnement de travail :**

**Sécurité :** Il (elle) sera basé/e à Hadjer Hadid avec des déplacements fréquents dans les zones d’intervention d’IRC.Le poste est non accompagné**.**

**Égalité des sexes :** L'IRC s'est engagé à réduire l'écart entre les sexes dans les postes de direction. Nous offrons des avantages qui permettent aux femmes de participer à la vie active, notamment un congé parental, des protocoles de sécurité tenant compte des spécificités des hommes et des femmes et d'autres avantages et allocations de soutien.

**L'IRC est un employeur soucieux de l'égalité des chances. L'IRC** examine tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans considération de race, de sexe, de couleur, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, d'état civil, de statut d'ancien combattant ou de handicap.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: SOUTH SUDAN -HUMAN RESSOURCES HEAD OF DEPARTMENT - JUBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/02/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:( 20.97$/hourly**): Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Associate Director, Global CRM (Salesforce)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees made to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

This position sits within Marketing Technology, the team that builds and runs the systems IRC uses to raise funds, engage supporters and advocate for the people we serve. These include the enterprise Salesforce CRM, our donation platforms, the global Rescue.org website and our email communications platforms. Together they underpin the fundraising, communications and advocacy work of External Relations around the world.

**Job Overview / Summary (What and Why):**

IRC’s Salesforce platform sits at the heart of how we raise funds and stay in touch with supporters. It manages a multi-million dollar fundraising operation, is used by around 500 staff, and runs as a single global, GDPR-compliant org built on a heavily customised Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP). We are now evaluating a potential move to Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, and exploring how AI, including Agentforce and integrations with models such as Anthropic’s Claude, can work responsibly inside the platform.

The Associate Director will lead that next chapter. Reporting to the Senior Director, Marketing Technology, the postholder owns the platform’s strategy, roadmap and architecture, and plays a central role in how Salesforce evolves at the IRC in the future.

The role brings together three things that rarely sit in one job: architect-level Salesforce judgement, leadership of a technical team, and a real understanding of how a global nonprofit raises and manages income. The postholder leads and develops the CRM team, holds contractors and delivery partners to clear standards of quality, security and supportability, and explains technical choices and trade-offs in plain language to senior leaders.

This is a team leadership role that stays close to the technology. We expect the postholder to spend most of their time on strategy, architecture and leading the team, while remaining hands-on where it matters: designing solutions, reviewing the team’s work and building when the situation calls for it.

**In their first year, the postholder will:**

- Get to know the current NPSP org in depth, including its customisations, integrations and technical debt, and the teams who depend on it.
- Agree a clear platform roadmap and the governance to deliver it with stakeholders across External Relations, Finance and programme teams.
- Identify where AI tools such as Agentforce can add real value, safely and in line with IRC’s data protection and AI governance requirements.
- Shape the team structure, ways of working and partner model the platform needs for its next phase.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Platform strategy and product ownership**

- Act as global product and platform owner for IRC’s Salesforce ecosystem, setting its direction and making the case for investment.
- Develop and maintain a prioritised CRM roadmap aligned with IRC’s fundraising, supporter engagement, finance and programme objectives, and run a fair, transparent process for managing demand.
- Lead IRC’s evaluation of Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, including the business case, options appraisal and, if approved, the migration strategy and plan.
- Lead the responsible evaluation and adoption of AI within the CRM ecosystem, including Agentforce and integrations with external AI models, identifying worthwhile use cases while meeting IRC’s data protection, security, ethical AI and governance requirements.
- Assess AppExchange and other third-party products and recommend what IRC should adopt, keep or retire.

**Architecture and technical leadership**

- Own the solution architecture of the platform: data model, automation, security model, integrations and managed packages, including NPSP, Account Engagement (Pardot), Outlook integration, Blackthorn and Apsona.
- Set design and build standards for declarative and programmatic development (Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, APIs), and review the work of the team and partners against them.
- Reduce technical debt in a heavily customised org, and make sure new work is simpler to support and ready for future platform changes.
- Oversee integrations with donation platforms, finance systems, the data warehouse and reporting tools, so that data flows are reliable and well documented.
- Stay hands-on: prototype, configure and build when that is the fastest way to unblock the team or prove an approach.

**Team and partner leadership**

- Lead, coach and develop a team of Salesforce administrators, developers and a business analyst, including recruitment, performance management, career development and workload planning.
- Build a team culture of good engineering practice, clear documentation and service to the people who use the platform.
- Manage contractors, implementation partners and suppliers, holding them to account for quality, cost and delivery, and contribute to procurement, licensing and budgeting.

**Governance, security and operations**

- Own platform governance: access management, security, audit controls, data quality, business continuity, and compliance with GDPR and other data protection requirements across countries.
- Oversee incident, problem, change and release management, including readiness for Salesforce’s three annual releases and managed-package updates.
- Oversee user support, testing and defect resolution delivered by the team and partners.
- Make sure reports and dashboards give leaders accurate, trusted information.

**Stakeholders and business context**

- Build strong relationships with fundraising, finance, data and programme leaders, and understand how IRC raises, processes and stewards income in different countries.
- Explain technical options, risks and trade-offs in plain language so that senior, non-technical stakeholders can make good decisions.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director, Marketing Technology

**Position directly supervises:** Team of Salesforce Admins/Developers/Business Analyst

**Other Internal and/or external contacts**:

**Internal***:* Close collaboration with global and regional stakeholders across External Relations, Resettlement, Asylum and Integration, Information Technology, Communications, Finance, Data and Analytics and other teams that rely on the CRM platform.

**External**: Technology suppliers, implementation partners, consultants, contractors and other service providers.

**Job Qualifications:**

**Education:**

**Minimum:**

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business systems or a related discipline or equivalent professional experience.

**Preferred:** Salesforce Architect-track certifications (e.g. Application Architect, System Architect), Nonprofit Cloud Consultant, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder or Platform Developer I/II.

**Work Experience:**

**Minimum:**

- Significant experience leading an enterprise Salesforce platform in a complex, multi-country organisation, with the architectural judgement to design and govern a large, heavily customised org.
- Experience acting as a product or platform owner, including developing roadmaps, governing demand and prioritising investment.
- Deep knowledge of Salesforce architecture, including data models, automation, security, integration and application lifecycle management, with enough hands-on fluency in declarative and programmatic development to guide and review the work of developers.
- Proven experience managing and developing a team of technical professionals, and overseeing contractors, consultants or delivery partners.
- An understanding of how nonprofits or comparable organisations raise and manage income (such as individual and recurring giving, gift processing and donor data) and how a CRM supports that work.
- Experience overseeing platform operations, including incident, change and release management.
- Experience working with APIs, ETL processes, integration platforms and cross-system data flows.
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to explain technical options and risks to non-technical and senior audiences.
- Experience of Agile delivery, using tools such as Git-based source control and Jira.
- Strong analytical thinking, judgement, problem solving ability and customer service orientation.

**Preferred:**

- Hands-on experience with Nonprofit Success Pack and Nonprofit Cloud, ideally including an NPSP-to-Nonprofit Cloud evaluation or migration.
- Experience delivering technology for fundraising, marketing, advocacy or supporter engagement teams.
- Familiarity with Salesforce Account Engagement (Pardot), Data Cloud, Agentforce or comparable marketing, data and AI platforms.
- Experience working with enterprise architecture, DevOps, Business Intelligence, Data Warehousing or integration technologies.
- Experience working with an international nonprofit, humanitarian or mission-led organisation.
- Experience running a CRM across multiple countries and currencies, including under GDPR and other data protection regimes.
- Experience contributing to supplier management, procurement, licensing, budgeting and technology business cases.
- Hands-on development experience with Apex, SOQL and Lightning Web Components.

  
**Working Environment*****:***

A collegiate environment working collaboratively across External Relations and broader IRC. Strong sense of transparency and accountability to ensure we are doing right by our clients and donors, exemplifying the IRC Way.

- This is a fully remote role, with travel 3–5 times per year for in-person time with the team and for learning and development.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, United Kingdom, and Kenya.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $113,102-$120,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £69,440-£84,058/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Country Director, Sudan
body:
Do you have the judgement, resilience, and leadership skills to guide an organisation through one of the world's most challenging operational environments?

Sudan presents an exceptionally complex humanitarian and development context. As Country Director, you will lead a dedicated team, navigate uncertainty and risk, build strong partnerships, and ensure that NCA continues to deliver meaningful programmes for communities affected by conflict and displacement.

We are looking for an experienced and grounded leader who can make sound decisions under pressure, **exercise prudence in complex and high-risk situations**, strengthen people and teams, and maintain strategic direction in a rapidly changing environment. Are you the leader we are looking for?

**About the position**

As Country Director, you will have overall responsibility for NCA's Sudan Country Programme and provide strategic leadership and oversight across programmes, operations, finance, security, and people management.

Reporting to the Head of Geographic Division for East Africa, you will lead a diverse Country Management Team and represent NCA in dialogue with authorities, donors, partners, and relevant coordination forums.

This is a senior leadership role combining strategic direction with the ability to navigate operational complexity, security risks, organisational change, and the realities of delivering humanitarian and development programmes in a conflict-affected context.

**Key responsibilities**

As Country Director, you will:

- Lead the strategic direction and implementation of NCA's Sudan Country Programme.
- Drive programme quality, impact, and accountability across the humanitarian and development portfolio.
- Lead and develop the Country Management Team and foster a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing organisational culture.
- Ensure effective security management, risk mitigation, safeguarding, and duty of care for staff and partners.
- Oversee financial management, compliance, resource allocation, and the organisational sustainability of the country programme.
- Represent NCA with donors, authorities, partners, and relevant coordination mechanisms.
- Identify opportunities and lead resource mobilisation efforts to sustain and develop the programme portfolio.
- Guide the organisation through change, uncertainty, and operational complexity while maintaining strategic focus.

**Qualifications and experience**

We are looking for a senior leader with substantial experience from international humanitarian and/or development work. You should have:

- A master's degree in international development, humanitarian action, political science, public administration, management, or another relevant field. Extensive and relevant professional experience may compensate for formal education.
- Significant senior leadership experience managing complex humanitarian and/or development programmes in fragile, conflict-affected, or high-risk environments.
- Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams, organisational change processes, and performance improvement.
- Proven experience with donor relations, resource mobilisation, financial oversight, risk management, and representation with senior external stakeholders.

Experience living and working in complex, fragile, or conflict-affected environments will be highly relevant. We also value a strong understanding of conflict sensitivity, localisation, and partnership-based programming.

Professional fluency in English is essential, while knowledge of Arabic is a significant advantage. You should also have strong digital literacy and be comfortable using technology for management, communication, and organisational oversight.

The position requires willingness and ability to undertake field travel in challenging operating environments and to live in shared accommodation in accordance with NCA's Sudan set-up.

**Personal qualities**

To succeed in this role, we believe you are:

**Strategic and decisive**

You make sound and timely decisions in complex and uncertain situations. You exercise strong judgement and balancing decisive action with careful consideration of security, financial, and organisational risks, while bringing conflictsensitivity to your decisions.

**A people-centred leader**

You invest in people and teams, build trust and accountability, and create the conditions for collaboration, learning, and strong performance.

**Resilient and adaptable**  
You remain composed and effective when circumstances change rapidly. You can navigate setbacks and uncertainty without losing sight of strategic priorities.

**A diplomatic and influential communicator**  
You build constructive relationships across cultures and stakeholder groups. You communicate with clarity and credibility and are comfortable representing the organisation at senior levels.

**What we offer**

This is an opportunity to lead one of NCA's most strategically important and challenging country programmes.

You will work alongside dedicated national and international colleagues and strong local partners to support communities affected by conflict, displacement, and crisis.

NCA offers a meaningful senior leadership role with significant responsibility and professional autonomy, as well as the opportunity to shape organisational impact in a highly dynamic environment. You will be part of a values-driven international organisation and supported by colleagues across NCA's country programmes and Head Office.

If you combine strategic leadership with resilience, **prudence, sound judgement, decisiveness, and a genuine commitment to people and partnerships**, we would like to hear from you.

**Ethical Commitments**

Norwegian Church Aid is committed to high standards of ethics and accountability in all that we do. As an employee, you will be required to sign the following documents when entering into an employment contract:

- **ACT Alliance Code of Conduct**
- **Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, Harassment, and Child Safeguarding Policy**

These are binding documents for all employees. We therefore ask you to familiarise yourself with them before applying. You can find the documents on our website: [https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet](https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet)

title: Research Manager for Venezuela, based in Caracas
Call for proposals: Ethiopia National Ecosystem Scoping Study
body:
## **Overview**

Elrha is commissioning an Ethiopia National Ecosystem Scoping Study to develop a robust, context-grounded understanding of the country’s climate-health-humanitarian ecosystem. The study will inform the longer-term programme of work for the HHCC, including priorities for evidence generation, innovation, partnerships and implementation.

Ethiopia has been selected as the pioneer national hub for the HHCC. The study will build on an earlier scoping exercise and generate deeper Ethiopia-specific evidence, innovation, stakeholder and implementation insights, rather than repeat the initial global scan.

The HHCC is a five-year initiative delivered by Elrha. It is designed as a lean, locally led platform connecting evidence generation, climate science and frontline humanitarian health implementation.

## **Objective**

The consultancy will provide the HHCC Anchor Institution, national multi-sectoral Steering Group and Elrha with evidence and analysis to shape the collaborative’s programme of work for Years 2–5. The work will:

- **Evidence and effective response gaps:** Assess what is known about climate-related health risks, effective responses, implementation barriers and evidence gaps in Ethiopia, while identifying existing work, networks and early warning tools that should be built upon.
- **Innovation opportunities:** Identify relevant existing and emerging innovations, including digital tools, early warning and anticipatory action mechanisms, community-led response models, service-delivery adaptations and financing approaches.
- **Stakeholder and ecosystem mapping:** Map relevant institutions, initiatives, tools, policies, local innovation actors, community intermediaries and grassroots structures across the climate-health-humanitarian nexus.
- **Recommendations for Years 2–5:** Recommend priority hazards, research themes, innovation opportunities and strategic partner configurations for the HHCC’s future programme of work.

## **Essential consultant specifications**

Applications are welcome from individual consultants, institutional research teams and collaborative teams. Applicants must demonstrate:

- **Qualifications:** A relevant postgraduate qualification in public health, epidemiology, environmental science, humanitarian assistance, health systems or a closely related discipline.
- **Experience:** At least five years of relevant research, situational analysis or public health programming experience in humanitarian, fragile or displacement settings, addressing climate-related vulnerabilities.
- **Ethiopia expertise:** Demonstrable knowledge of Ethiopia’s public health, disaster management, innovation and humanitarian systems, with access to relevant institutions and networks.
- **Methods:** Experience in rigorous evidence synthesis, stakeholder mapping and semi-structured key informant interviews in complex settings.
- **Language and communication:** Excellent written English and report-writing capability, with fluency in Amharic within the field interview team. Familiarity with other Ethiopian languages is desirable.
- **National research involvement:** The substantive involvement of national researchers based in Ethiopia is mandatory. International teams must formally partner with an Ethiopian researcher or local research institution and demonstrate joint design and substantive delivery responsibility.

## **Timeline**

- **RFP issued:** 2 November 2026
- **Application deadline:** 20 November 2026, 5:00 pm UTC
- **Expected contract start and inception meeting:** January 2027

title: Research Manager for Nigeria, based in Abuja
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the PANDA Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT operates through three Initiatives: REACH, PANDA, and AGORA. This recruitment opportunity pertains to the PANDA Initiative.

PANDA is IMPACT’s lever on humanitarian aid responses which focusing on improving outcomes for beneficiaries through direct engagement with partners and their activities. Where REACH works through soft power and partnerships to affect systemic change, PANDA is direct action that allows us to ensure that system and its participants are trustworthy and delivering the most effective, efficient and equitable response possible. PANDA is praxis – it is how IMPACT manifests our vision of acting as a catalyst of change within the aid community to work through focused or multidimensional analysis of projects, programmes and policies to identify their results, strengths and weaknesses, and how they can be improved, then proposes or implements a concrete plan for improvement.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to support our team in Nigeria.**

**Department**: PANDA

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Location**: Abuja, Nigeria (with occasional stays in Dakar, Senegal)

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Nigeria is among the world's most critical hunger hotspots, where protracted conflict, displacement, economic pressures, and climate shocks are driving rapidly worsening humanitarian needs. In the Northeast, more than 8.8 million people require urgent assistance, including 4.9 million children, sustained displacement, protection risks, severe funding shortfalls, a growing nutrition emergency, and a cholera outbreak. Food insecurity is expected to reach record levels, with an estimated 34.7 million people nationwide projected to face Crisis-level food insecurity or worse by August 2026. Meanwhile, the Northwest faces a different but equally severe crisis driven by chronic poverty, banditry, communal violence, and recurrent flooding, which have displaced hundreds of thousands of people (800,000 IOM DTM R18), damaged livelihoods and farmland, and contributed to sharp declines in agricultural production. Together, these overlapping shocks are undermining resilience, increasing humanitarian needs, and threatening both current food security and future harvests.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. Historically, IMPACT Initiatives has been present in both the Northeast and Northwest of Nigeria. Thematically, across 2021 – 2023 IMPACT Initiatives fielded [Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7b6cde65/REACH_NGA_TOR_MSNA-Northwest_March-2022-1.pdf) (MSNAs), [Hard to Reach](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/0f980ce2/NGA-1809_Situation_Overview_Q1_Feb_Mar_2022.pdf) (H2R) assessments, [Area Based Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7cddc3c2/REACH_NGA_TOR_Rapid_Area-Based_Assessments_in_Areas_of_Return_February_2021.pdf) (ABA), [Rapid Overviews of Areas of Return](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/07db0c79/REACH_NGA_ToR_Rapid_Overview_Of_Areas_Of_Return_ROAR_-Feb-2022.pdf) (ROAR), [Thematic Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/9fa6a7cf/REACH_NGA_Brief_assessment-of-H2R-Gujba-and-Tarmua-LGA_April-2022.pdf) (TA), [Rapid Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/6b1d770d/REACH_NGA_Yobe_Floods_Brief.pdf) (RA), and [WASH Infrastructure Mapping](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/afb497ac/REACH_NGA_Factsheet_WASH-Infrastructure-Maiduguri_May-2021.pdf), while also playing a key role in Famine Monitoring, Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance, and the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI). Since 2026, IMPACT has reintroduced the MSNA, Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), JMMI and other thematic assessments in Nigeria in addition to the HARP TPM project which has been running since 2024.

## **PROJECT PRFILE**

The position is recruited for the Third-Party Monitoring (TPM) Project covering FCDOs Humanitarian and Resilience Programme (HARP) Facility. For this programme, IMPACT is in partnership with FACT Foundation. While in Nigeria, staff shall be hosted by FACT Foundation and for his or her mission, the Research Manager will fall under the direct responsibility and management of FACT and their delegates for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by FACT’s Security, HR, Administration, and Logistics rules and regulations, and in coordination with FACT, ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the management of the Country Representative, the Research Manager oversees the research activities and staff within the purview of the FCDO-funded Third Party Monitoring (TPM) Project. The Research Manager shall oversee and execute all research activities within the above-mentioned Project, meeting quarterly deliverables in a timely fashion while ensuring that the quality of research remains high. S/he will moreover liaise extensively with counterparts from Fact Foundation who are IMPACT’s partners in the Consortium for the Project, while supporting the Country Representative in stakeholder engagement with FCDO’s Implementing Partners.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager responsibilities include the following:

***Strategy development & implementation***

- With specific attention to the FCDO-funded TPM Project’s, and while supervised by the CR, the RM is to ensure that IMPACT has an up to date understanding of the country’s socio-economic situation, the impact of a crisis and the aid/humanitarian situation, as well as the humanitarian planning, coordination, response mechanism developments, and key humanitarian stakeholders.
- For the TPM Project, **develop and oversee the implementation of the project’s strategy**. Specifically, during the inception period, in conjunction with the CR, set out the project’s overall strategy, develop concomitant workplans for each staff member, and put in place the requisite structures for the staff members such that each individual has clarity as to how to work towards the common goal of completing deliverables in a timely manner and at a high standard, and ultimately supplying impact to FCDO and Implementing Partners at the outcome level.

## ***Research Planning***

- For the TPM Project, ensure that all the research is planned in line with the relevant project and programme objectives, as well as the Project and Country Strategy. This is to include:
- Ensure that all research complies with IMPACT’s HQ Research Department guidelines and standards.
- Ensure that al necessary Secondary Data Reviews are conducted and integrated into the research.
- Ensure that research ToRs are validated by HQ prior to the commencement of data collection.
- Ensure that research ToRs are understood by the team and updated accordingly.
- Keep track of progress and delays of all assigned assessments throughout the research cycle.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to include their two assessment and data staff in the research.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation to ensure that the portion of the research carried out by them is validated by IMPACT HQ.
- Where necessary, proactively support the team by conducting research (research design. ToRs, tool building, data management, data analysis, product drafting).
- While supported by the CR, conduct dissemination and stakeholder meetings with FCDO and Implementing Partners.

***Research Implementation***

- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to **ensure that the data is collected in the fashion and format that allows IMPACT to clean and analyse the data**.
- Ensure that all collected data is stored **in line with IMPACT’s Data Management Guidelines**, as well as with the data management plan Annex in the Research ToR.
- Ensure that data is revised and cleaned, **with all revisions recorded** as per IMPACT data management guidelines.
- **Oversee all the analyses of the collected data**, as stipulated in the Research ToRs.
- Ensure that data and its analysis **do not contain personal information** and are validated by IMPACT HQ, before sharing to external parties.
- Supervise and where necessary support the team with the analysis and drafting of the information products.
- **Review all products** before they are sent to the CR or IMPACT HQ for validation.
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ **before release to FCDO and Implementing Partners**.

***Team Management and Leadership***

- Ensure that all staff members understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities, as well as their reporting and validation duties to HQ.
- Ensure that all staff members have **clear and regularly updated ToRs, Workplans, and Key performance Indicators (KPIs)** against which their performance will be appraised.
- **Promote team building, productivity, and staff welfare**.
- Mentor and support the team **to build capacities, improve efficiency and performance**.
- **Promote the growth and development of staff** within the organisation, actively linking with HQ to provide feedback and support retention and internal mobility. Identify capacity building opportunities for growth, proactively provide high-performing staff with opportunities to surge (a short-term deployment to another mission) and develop pathways for junior staff to grow and move into management or specialist positions.
- **Ensure communication and linkages with HQ** are made immediately in case of the occurrence of an HR-related problem.

***Internal Coordination and Communication***

- Facilitate clear and seamless communication within the IMPACT TPM team across Senegal and Nigeria, as well as the FACT Foundation team in Nigeria.
